question
Isn't there a possibility that the AI could skew it when it collects the opinions of many people and puts them together?
Of course there is that.
Related question: is there a bias in the LLM?
Diverse biases by LLMs.
[Ask Qarasu-14B a question]
But is there no bias if it is put together by a human being? Of course, humans have biases.
So this is not an "AI or human" issue.
Issues that should be resolved by creating mechanisms such as making the process open and verifiable by a third party
Related question: will AI be a black box?
[Reasoning model] works by verbalizing and outputting the thinking process, and is less of a black box than a person who thinks silently.
Research is also underway to examine the internal firing of the model during task execution. This is like sticking electrodes into the brain if you were to use a human analogy.
Stabbing electrodes into public officials is ethically difficult, but disclosing the internal state of AI in public service will be possible in the future.
If you think being a black box is a problem, you'd rather use AI instead of humans.
Not all people can think and speak out about politics, what do we do with those who don't?
Some radical views like [unconscious data democracy] are not in favor of it.
The current lack of opportunities for people to have their opinions heard and to feel good about expressing them is the reason why the ability to think and express opinions is not developed.
Especially [minors do not have the right to vote], and when they come of age, they are suddenly told they should vote, which is absurd.
In Taiwan, systems such as JOIN created opportunities for students to voice their opinions from the student stage.
[High School Students' Suggestions Led to Institutional Improvements at JOIN in Taiwan]
Similar clusters were seen in [Shin Tokyo 2050 Broad Listening
Today's major social networking sites are marked by people with radical opinions.
Most people don't want to argue with radicals.
The [pro-social media] mindset is designed to draw attention to "[Bridging Opinions]" that are favored by those in different opinion clusters.

pages.title: What happened with the "new section on Advancing the Human Rights Situation?"

lines.text: What happened with the "new section on Advancing the Human Rights Situation?"

Among the PRs of [initiative taken by the government in the formulation of a policy or bill (rather than by bureaucrats) to promote good governance], only one PR received over 100 comments at most. of the 10 or so comments at most, only one received more than 100 comments.
https://github.com/team-mirai/policy/pull/6335
What's going on, I asked o3.
[o3.icon]

The following is a report on why PR 6335 "Establishment of a new section on the advancement of the human rights situation" has become a "hot topic" in a short period of time, based on publicly available information. To summarize just the main points: (1) The proposal included a large amount of highly abstract information on "human rights," a topic that involves a high degree of value judgment, and received criticism from both legal and technical experts at the same time. (2) Before the rules for discussion on GitHub were in place, the number of comments from outside parties increased, and the comments snowballed from the first day. --The result was a three-tiered structure.
[nishio.icon]

In short, it is an understanding that this is what happens when a highly abstract discussion is posted in a place that is not supposed to be a discussion forum, and then spread on social networking sites.
(Personally, I think it would have been a good idea to move to PUBLIC ARCHIVE at the end of the Upper House election, which was actually delayed by a few days.)
Team Mirai staff did not participate in this discussion, so calling this an "internal Team Mirai discussion" is misinformation.
If you put something on a bulletin board that anyone can write on, it's like a third-party fight broke out there.
I think any engineer familiar with GitHub knows that "anyone can write on it."
Worse, some users were using Yasuno-san's face icon, which some may have misidentified as him.
[https://gyazo.com/14da80758bb3e832dd1f76a6dbb2d198]

Note as an example of failure of a large scale deliberation (well, it was just a [Web BBS] state without AI moderators like they had put in during the Tokyo gubernatorial election because they didn't expect to start a discussion there, so it was vulnerable, I guess).
Continuation of o3 description
1. the content of PR and the specific fire of the "technology party
1-1 Outline of Proposal
Through a dialogue between the proposer (Akio Hoshi) and an AI chatbot, he tried to add a new section to the manifesto called "Advancement of the Human Rights Situation"

Criticisms of "jurisprudential imprecision" and "loss of intellectual property in redefinition" erupted because of the ambiguous connection between human rights and international and domestic law, while positioning human rights as "norms".
1-2 Direct causes of the stormy discussion
Major Points of Controversy Examples of Typical Comments
Treatment of enforceability of international human rights law and Article 98 of the Constitution "Japan has not ceded its authority to the UN", etc.
Engineering users: Implementation should be prioritized over "norms"; language is abstract; "Moving code is as good as police power", etc.
Philosophy/Humanities Users: The redefinition of the concept of human rights, History of Enlightenment thought "Misunderstanding the flow from Magna Carta," etc.
Thus, July 14 → over 100 comments as of July 24, an unusually long time even for the party's repository!
2. diffusion dynamics - "X influencer cannon
2-1 Diffusion time line
Around 20:00 on 7/14 | Create PR → Start discussion in GitHub
7/15 am | Post by Akio Hoshi (IT x human rights journalist) with link to X
7/15 same day | Retweeted by author Taiyo Fujii
7/15 evening | Researcher Sayaka Oki described the thread as a "dangerous discussion
7/16-17 | also reprinted in Threads and Bluesky
7/18-19 | note.com and other outside media critique articles
2-2 Impact
Hoshi's post received 12,000 likes and over 3,000 reposts (from a report with screenshots), and the number of new visitors to GitHub PR skyrocketed.
Technical clusters with overlapping social graphs flowed in at once, and the "anyone can write" mechanism made the volume of discussion uncontrollable.
In the GitHub comment section, the "discuss here instead of X" and "explain in X" groups clashed, and the meta-discussion accelerated.
3. secondary wave: media and critics' arguments
note The article "Selectivism and Dystopia" makes the debate more visible by mentioning the danger of a controlled society while the proposal calls for "inclusion of the weak.
The position of "Team Mirai = Tech x Human Rights" was reexamined on YouTube political feeds and blogs, and began to spill over into the party image.
4. summary - three reasons for the expansion of the problem
Difficulty in setting the theme
The cost of shared assumptions is high due to the intersection of jurisprudence, ethics, and implementation.
Vulnerability of Open Draft Method
The operational rules that made GitHub a "plaza" were not yet in place and could not withstand the surge of inbound traffic.
External pressure through influencer diffusion

Tens of thousands of reaches were reached overnight, and participants with varying degrees of understanding, both inside and outside the party, commented simultaneously. As a result, discussions diverged on multiple topics, including "What are human rights?" and "What is the boundary between politics and code?

This case is a typical example of the combination of difficulty of the content itself, social proliferation, and immaturity in process design, which resulted in a short period of time in which the situation could not be resolved.

lines.text: Findings from Team Mirai's social experiment "Talkable Manifesto
[Findings from Team Mirai's social experiment "Talkable Manifesto"｜NISHIO Hirokazu https://note.com/nishiohirokazu/n/nb35e8d526fd4?sub_rt=share_pb]

Findings from [Team Mirai]'s social experiment "[Talkable Manifesto]".
[IIDOBATA system]
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378258449342603] I wrote an article summarizing insights from the Broad Listening project run by Anno Takahiro’s political party, Team Mirai. #Pluarlity

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378411453366579] 1/  New article: What we learned from Team Mirai’s “Talking Manifesto,” a large-scale Broad Listening experiment during Japan’s 2025 election. Thread
> #TeamMirai #DigitalDemocracy #BroadListening

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378521935319490] 2/ In May 2025, AI engineer Takahiro Anno founded Team Mirai and won a seat in the Upper House (≈2.6% vote share). That secured national party status and stable public funding for digital public goods for 6 years.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378786059333692] 3/ True to its pledge, Team Mirai formed an engineering team to build digital public goods—an innovation in how we finance “the commons,” echoing dialogues seen at Funding the Commons and ideas from Audrey Tang & Glen Weyl’s “Plurality." #Plurality #FundingTheCommons

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378863049875956] 4/ Context: In the 2024 Tokyo gubernatorial race, Anno popularized Broad Listening—using AI to collect, structure, and reflect diverse public input. He placed 5th (154,638 votes; 2.3%)—remarkable for an unaffiliated newcomer.
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379016988971494] 5/ 2024 introduced 3 connected projects:
> ① AI Town Hall (24/7 Q&A, even by phone)
> ② Broad Listening visualization
> ③ Open-source policy improvement on GitHub
> —AI referenced the manifest on GitHub; insights were visualized at scale.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379104167829713] 6/ During the 2024 campaign window (Jun 21–Jul 6): 232 problem reports, 104 change proposals, 85 adopted; the AI answered ~8,600 questions using the latest policy data. This volume would’ve been hard without these systems.
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379165543080375] 7/ 2025 upgrade: “Talking Manifesto.”
> Voters chat with an AI interviewer that helps them articulate concerns → the AI files a GitHub pull request (PR) on their behalf. No GitHub skills required.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379291045089687] 8/ Impact landed immediately. Within days, >10× more proposals than the governor race. Ultimately, 8.5k+ policy suggestions arrived—an unprecedented PR inflow for a political organization.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379390093275557] 9/ Challenge 1 —Throughput: I built a daily GitHub-Actions pipeline to pull PR data and auto-classify by target files for rapid triage and debate with LLMs. It hit API rate limits at 1k/hr, so we moved to diff-only, incremental updates.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379511359074498] 10/ Challenge 2 —Triage UX: Jun Ito’s auto-labeling let staff filter PRs by domain (health, education, etc.), routing to the right specialists directly in GitHub’s UI.
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379655798497447] 11/ Challenge 3 —Ops at scale: With
> http://
> Devin.ai, we demoed Slack-native commands to query all proposals and auto-generate reports in minutes—useful when the dataset ballooned.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379752116293643] 12/ Unexpected UX pitfall: Many people chatted on the index (README) page and submitted proposals there—asking about or changing content that actually lived on subpages (e.g., “Health”). The UI nudged them to the wrong place.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379890700554641] 13/ Fix to consider next time: If a user types on the index page, search across sections before answering; if they propose edits there, redirect them to the most relevant section first. (Hard to back-fit mid-campaign, but key learning.)

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973380164735111276] 14/ Visualization: We used our upgraded Broad Listening tool “Kouchou-AI” (born from “Talk to the City”) to map proposals and spot patterns. Server-side analysis produced shareable URLs so policy & comms teams could act fast. #TalkToTheCity #KouchouAI

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973380259656380709] 15/ Re-clustering effect: Observing real voter input led us to add a new “Welfare” category and reassign many items. Broad Listening doesn’t just collect opinions—it reshapes the taxonomy of policy.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973380336907149736] 16/ We then extracted problem statements from proposals and built a hierarchical map (e.g., “Inclusive education & welfare,” “Transparent, composable policymaking”). Each node links back to its source PR.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973380442846879801] 17/ Biggest structural pain: PR conflicts. Multiple edits to the same lines can’t be merged simultaneously. Staff had to read conflicting edits and synthesize fresh ones—a heroic but unsustainable approach. Next time: collect problems & goals, not line-edits.

pages.title: On the Theoretical Limitations of Embedding-Based Retrieval

lines.text: On the Theoretical Limitations of Embedding-Based Retrieval
[Theoretical Limitations of Embedding-Based Search
https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.21038
[Dense search]

>[hillbig https://x.com/hillbig/status/1962280460605862194] Although [retrieval by embedded vectors] has become popular in information retrieval, it has been shown to have theoretical limitations. That is, there is a limit to the number of document combinations that can be represented by the dimensionality d of the query and document vectors, indicating that there are "search tasks that can never be represented".

> This limit can only be obtained if the degrees of freedom of the inner product matrix between documents and queries, expressed in the mathematical concept of sign-rank, d, is made quite large. For example, a 4k dimensional embedding cannot represent a document set of several hundred million or so (the search targets are often billions to tens of billions of documents).

> We also designed a LIMIT dataset with a hypothetical problem set that is realistic and flexible. It consists of a who likes what document and a "who likes apples" query, covering all top-k combinations. Even with the latest embedding, very few RECALLs were given.

> On the other hand, it was difficult with embedding, but can be solved with cross-encoders (do they encode and score both query and document at the same time?) and relanguages using them, and multi-vector, sparse models can also be solved.
> Current academic benchmarks measure only a fraction of the query space and may over-learn (including problems that are essentially unsolvable, as above)
> Comments

> Although the versatility of embedded vectors is widely used in information retrieval, from keyword search and full-text search, it has limitations as described above. There is a limitation because neighborhood search is pushed into a finite d-dimensional vector space (you can't push a complex traffic network into a 2-dimensional map).

lines.text: People who think they are arguing as equals on social networking sites.
When Mr. A posts on a social networking site and Mr. B replies to it
Excluding cases where Mr. A and Mr. B are originally acquainted.
In other words, it is assumed that "I received a mentions from [stranger] B" from Mr. A's point of view.
Sometimes Mr. B perceives that he is "arguing [equally] with Mr. A".
I wondered "how did this happen?" regarding specific cases, so I let GPT explain.
[GPT5.icon]
In this case, B's self-perception of "arguing as equals" shows some cognitive distortions and leaps in assumptions.

Especially in a social networking environment, this proceeds without confirming the other party's consent or willingness to participate, so even if the person thinks they are "equal," in reality it is asymmetrical.
Problems with B's cognition
1. omit "consent to initiate discussion"
Equal discussion presupposes that both parties are willing to engage in discussion.
This time, B is participating in a situation in which A is not in discussion mode, and sees it as a "debate forum" on its own.
For A, it was a "sudden request for dispute" and he did not remember entering the ring.
In sports, this is like starting a game next to the opponent warming up.
2. set the "stage conditions for discussion" on your own
B proceeds with the story based on his own criteria (practical and institutional viewpoints) and mistakenly assumes that "A is also on that stage".
In fact, A is speaking in layers of mathematical definitions and the stage conditions do not match.
This is similar to the "playing different board games at the same table" situation.
3. misinterpretation of "relational symmetry".
A does not know B, but B reads A's transmission and approaches.
The relationship is one-sided and the sharing of knowledge and intentions is asymmetrical.
Despite this, B believes that it is an "equal playing field".
This is typical of misinterpreting a one-sided call as a "mutually agreed upon conversation.
4. short-circuit of "[no discussion] = lack of ability or willingness on the part of the other party
B spits out the "not controversial" assessment externally.
The reason it is not established, however, is not a lack of understanding of A, but a mismatch of assumptions and modes.
This is a [cause attribution error] (imputing a cause to the nature of the other party).
To sum up.
B's perception of "equal discussion" is,
Discussion begins without consensus
Imposition of stage conditions
Ignoring relational asymmetries
fallacy of causal attribution
and includes complex distortions such as
Thus, even though B "thinks" he is having a fair debate, it is in fact a surprise one-sided intervention for A, and is not structurally equal.

[nishio.icon]Begin your initial discussion with "A had premise PA, leading to conclusion XA; B had premise PB, leading to conclusion XB." and explain what kind of exchange you were having at this level of abstraction, starting with.
[GPT5.icon]
Roger. We will break this down at the PA/PB, XA/XB abstraction level.
appearance on stage
A: From premise PA (i.e., the evaluation depends on the chosen criterion K) to conclusion XA (i.e., the apparent difference is only a difference in "which K" is used to measure it).

B: Assumption PB (= reasonable if measured by the third criterion K₃ / furthermore, the reality constraint C works) to conclusion XB (= the ordinal is almost invariant regardless of how K₃ is chosen).
Flow of exchange (abstract)
1. A→XA
A stands on PA and states that "the comparison of the subject is K-dependent" (declarative sharing, little intent to start a discussion).
You don't explain PA here.[nishio.icon]
2. B→PB, XB
B introduces another premise PB, "Let's measure by K₃," and presents XB (which appears to be an argument against A, but actually replaces the basis of the comparison).
3. noting the variable nature of A to PB
A tuts from PA's point of view that "even in a PB frame, the result is driven by the choice of K₃" (reaffirming the K-dependence).
Pointing out that "even if it's PB, it's still XA."[nishio.icon]
4. add B to PB + C to reinforce XB
B implicitly adds on the real constraints C (e.g., equilibrium, arbitrage, and institutions) and strengthens XB by saying that "in practice, differences due to K₃ are negligible".
5. pointed out that the discussion of "A→"C premise" is out of scope.
A points out that his story is the scope of the mathematical layer called PA; XB is a claim of another layer that includes C. PB to XB cannot stand in general without C. Organized.
6. further movement of B to premise (PB2)
B brings up the cause of stabilization and the institution (PB2) to explain the validity of XB in practical terms.
(Here, the issue slides from "definitional issues" to "actual mechanism issues")
7. a -> Restatement of issue fixation
A clarifies that he is only talking about definitions and measurements based on PA; does not get on PB+C+PD; clarifies layer discrepancy.
8. criticized B for not discussing the issue on an equal footing in an air rip.
What was happening (pattern)
Non-sharing of premises: A adopted PA and B adopted PB (+ C, PD in the middle), speaking different propositions with the same word ("risk", etc.).
Replacement of the foundation: B is in the form of a "rebuttal," but the evaluation function and condition set are actually changed (i.e., the problem set is made different).
Layer misalignment: A = actuarial definition / B = practical system. Only the conclusions clash without the layers intersecting.
Initiation of debate without consensus: A is considered a shared post, B is considered a debate. Mode disagreement triggers emotional evaluation (e.g., "it's not a debate").
If you want to converge (abstract temp)
1. specify the previously agreed-upon assumption set P* (treatment of K and whether it includes C or PD).
2. determine proposition M (what is the "comparison") under P*.
3. note the difference in range by juxtaposing XA under PA and XB under PB(+C,PD) as "separate theorems".
In short, A is making a "formal claim of K-dependence" and B is making a "practical claim involving C and PD," and since the premises are different, the conclusions also differ.

pages.title: Justice and rejection sensitivity in children and adolescents with ADHD symptoms

lines.text: Justice and rejection sensitivity in children and adolescents with ADHD symptoms
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00787-014-0560-9
[GPT5.icon]
Paper abstract (Bondü & Esser, 2015)

Theme: In 10-19 year olds with ADHD tendency, how [justice sensitivity (JS)] and [rejection sensitivity (RS)] are related to comorbid problems (depression, behavior problems, self-esteem low self-esteem).

Subjects/measures: 1,235 German schoolchildren; ADHD symptoms, JS (3 perspectives: victim, observer, and perpetrator), frequency of unfair perception, RS (anxious and angry types), depression, behavior problems, and self-esteem measured by questionnaire.
Key Results:
Participants with ADHD symptoms had higher victim JS, [perception of unfairness], and anxiety/anger RS, and lower perpetrator JS.
Latent variable path analysis showed that JS and RS partially mediate the association between ADHD symptoms → comorbid problems.

Implication: In ADHD support, there is significance in incorporating psychoeducational and CBT interventions (e.g., reevaluation of interpretations, relearning social cues) that work on sensitivity to "unfairness" and sensitivity to rejection. *Causality cannot be determined due to the cross-sectional nature of the study.
Terminology Positioning

Justice Sensitivity (JS): a characteristic of how often one perceives injustice and how strongly one reacts to it. Standard to measure from multiple perspectives of victim/observer/perpetrator. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7868537/])

[Rejection Sensitivity] (RS): the tendency to anticipate rejection anxiously/angry and react strongly (Downey & Feldman model). ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8714401/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9768487/?utm _source=chatgpt.com])
Related Research Map (representative examples)

JS x Aggression: victim JS and RS associated with elevated reactive/instrumental aggression, perpetrator JS associated with inhibitory direction. Confirmed in a large sample. ([PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25136820/])
[Reactive and instrumental attacks]

JS/RS x Depression (longitudinal): youth with higher depression show higher victim JS and (anxiety/angry) RS, an association that persists across time (N=1,665, at time 2). ([Frontiers https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.01446/full?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28955257/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Interrelationships among multiple "susceptibility" traits: JS, RS, [provocation susceptibility], [moral aversion susceptibility], etc. are bundled and correlated in ego-orientation/other-orientation and linked to [aggression] via hostility attribution bias and anger traits. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4884733/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[Sensitivity to provocation and moral aversion]

ADHD and Social Feedback/RS: Young ADHD tendency is associated with hypersensitivity to [Social Feedback] and self-reported RS (task/neurophysiological indicators). ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6395560/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30155685/? utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Measurement development of JS: English adaptation of the simplified JSS-8 (distinguishing between "fundamentalist JS" and "opportunistic JS"). ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10627457/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Reading Points/Practical Tips

Profile asymmetry: important in that it is easy to be "victim JS↑/perpetrator JS↓" in ADHD. Over-detection of injustice and underestimation of the perpetrator of self can occur simultaneously. This is easily connected to peer relationship friction -> depression/behavior problems. ([PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24878677/])
Intervention Design:

There is a theoretical basis for cognitive reassessment (training not to assume that ambiguous cues = hostility) and rereading of social cues to lower hostility attribution bias and reduce aggression. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4884733/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Responding to RS (monitoring rejection anticipation, attention shifting, strengthening supportive relationships) is effective in secondary prevention of depression/anxiety. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3733267/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Supplemental: Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria (RSD) is a concept widely discussed in party and qualitative research, but it is not a diagnostic name and research accumulation is ongoing. There is a growing body of qualitative data on experiences with and making sense of criticism and rejection. ([PLOS https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0263366&utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm .nih.gov/articles/PMC10569543/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

1. in an open communal space, a participant posts a lengthy, professional proposal and commentary.
2. another participant shares procedural information to the effect that "proposals are no longer being accepted".

8. the operational decision was ultimately upheld and the norms were confirmed, but the friction in the relationship remained.
General principles that worked behind the scenes
Common ground of attention: readability of public space is a common resource. Long and individual repartee leads to wear and tear, and norms are triggered.
Lack of explicit norms: If the rules are unclear, procedural unfairness is likely to occur.
Intent ≠ Impact: Even well-intentioned advice can create a backlash if taken as a relational message.
Sensitivity mismatch: If sensitivity to rejection or provocation is high, ambiguous pointers are over-detected as aggression/rejection, leading to reactive aggression.
Legitimacy of sanctions depends on procedures: public attention has high face costs, and proportionality, sequence, and clarity of explanation determine acceptability.
Summary in one line

The clash between "freedom of individual expression" and "legibility of the place and procedural fairness" turned into a public escalation due to the meshing of relational frames and sensitivities - an event.

The side with higher [Rejection Sensitivity] (RS) is more likely to over-detect ambiguous attention as a rejection signal.

lines.text: Put the first big stone in.
It's a common metaphor, so I'll generate it later.
[GPT5.icon]
A typical "Big Rocks" story goes like this.
1. demonstration in class/training
The instructor prepares a clear glass jar and (1) a large stone, (2) a pebble, and (3) sand (some versions use (4) water).
First, the "big stone" is placed in a jar. It looks full.
Next, put a "pebble" in and shake it, it goes into the gap and still goes in.
And when more "sand" is added, more goes in.
(In the pouring version) water also enters at the end.
2. questions from the lecturer
What is the lesson of this experiment?"
Students tend to answer, "You can get a lot in depending on how you pack it," but the instructor corrects them.
3. the real lesson

'What I really want to tell you is that if you don't put the big stones (the most important things) in first, you won't be able to put them in later.' If you fill it with small errands (pebbles/sand) first, you can't put in the important stuff."
4. correspondence of interpretations
Bottle = my time, attention, and resources (24 hours a day or operating this month).
Large stones = most important tasks directly related to value/goals (family time, deep work, health, etc.).
Pebbles = necessary but less important task.
Sand and water = chore, notification, and inertia.
5. attention to common misunderstandings
This is not "all-in magic". If there are too many big rocks, they won't fit. It is essential to narrow down the number first and place the scheduled blocks first (put them on the calendar first).
To drop it into practice, the standard usage is "decide on up to three large stones for the week and reserve time first → place the remaining pebbles/sand around them".
[GPT5.icon]
The oldest verifiable source in print is "[First Things First]" (1994) by [Stephen R. Covey] et al. In the same book, the "Big Rocks" demonstration story is used.
It was later widely disseminated through FranklinCovey's training materials and videos (a.k.a. "Big Rocks").
[nishio.icon] Isn't there one in [Seven Habits]?
[GPT5.icon]

There are none. The so-called "big stone, pebble, sand, and water bottle" demonstration does not appear in the text of The Seven Habits (1989). Covey elaborated on this metaphor later in First Things First (1994), which contains the demonstration story.
It is often introduced in the context of "Prioritize the Highest Priority (Habit 3)" along with training and videos, and is often associated with the "7 Habits".

What's new.
GraphRAG formulation:
1.[G-Indexing] (graph construction and indexing)
2.[G-Retrieval] (Retrieval of node/triple/path/subgraph)
3.[G-Generation] (Generate acquisition graph as input)
Utilizes relational knowledge and global structures that are difficult to pick up in string RAGs, and is advantageous in QFS, etc.
G-Indexing (graph infrastructure)
Data source: open KG (Wikidata/ConceptNet, etc.) / own construction (TAG from documents, tables, logs).

NG is [Knowledge Graph].

Index:
Graph Indexing (Structure Search)
Text index (Template conversion → BM25/dense search)
Vector index (node/egonet embedding)
Hybrid recommended.
G-Retrieval
Retrievers: non-parametric (BFS/shortest path/PCST), LM systems, GNN systems, or combined.
Paradigm: batch/repeat (adaptive/non-adaptive)/multi-stage (coarse to fine).
Granularity: node, triple, path, subgraph, mixed.
Enhancement: query expansion/decomposition, knowledge merge/pruning (re-ranking, PageRank, LLM checks, etc.)
G-Generation
Generator:
GNN (strong in discrimination tasks)
LM (strong in generation/reasoning)
Hybrid: cascade (GNN to LM prefix)/parallel (representation coupling and output integration).
LM input format for graphs:
Graph language (edge tables, natural sentences, code-like notation, syntax trees, node sequences)
Graph embedding (fused by Prefix/Prompt Tuning or FiD).
Generation enhancement: pre (rewriting and planning) / during (constraint decoding, etc.) / post (answer integration and verification).
learning
No learning required: rule search + prompts, embedded similarity.
With learning: Supervision/remote supervision/RL/self-supervision to optimize the retriever/generator.
Collaborative learning: mutual reinforcement for alternate learning and integration purposes.
Application and evaluation
Tasks: KBQA/CSQA, EL/RE, fact verification, link prediction, dialogue, recommendation.
Areas: e-commerce, medical, academic, legal, literary, etc.
Bench: WebQSP/CWQ/HotpotQA, etc., STaRK, GraphQA, GRBENCH, CRAG.
Indicators: EM/F1/Accuracy/BLEU types + acquisition quality (coverage, diversity, fidelity).
Industry Case Studies
Microsoft GraphRAG (QFS enhanced with community summary), NebulaGraph Edition, Ant Group Edition, Neo4j NaLLM/Graph Builder, etc.
Future Issues
Dynamic graph updating and adaptation, multimodal integration, and efficiency in large graphs,
Linkage with Graph Foundation Models, lossless compression to mitigate long-text problems, standard bench maintenance, and application extensions.
Practical tips (super summary)
Hybrid indexing + multi-stage acquisition for accuracy/cost optimization even on a small scale.
Select granularity (path/subgraph center) according to the task.
LM input should be in short, complete, readable graph language (community summary if necessary).
Critical phases are stabilized when re-ranking/pruning and post-verification are included.

"Bottom-up tagging" super-summary (3 lines)
Instead of a pre-designed classification tree, a knowledge network is developed by adding links (=tags) that spontaneously arise from the memos.
This is a practice that transplants the KJ method's "nameplate creation/convergence" to digital and turns the cumulative effect of ideas (underdevelopment → stability → inclusion → downfall).
Scrapbox/Cosense emphasizes "divergence = branching/convergence = links across branches" in a lincographic manner, with page links and row links at the core.

Core Principles (excerpts)
Top-down classification is minimal: assumption that structure changes with additional knowledge. Fixed trees lead to "dead text". Store in a network.
Linking is the tag: [[page link]] rather than #hash, and use line links to establish a concrete relationship. Do not break references just by copying them.
Visualize moments of convergence: lines connecting different groups = convergent thinking (critical backlink). This is the point of progress of knowledge.
Life cycle of ideas:
Undeveloped (hypothetical sprout) → Stable (reappearance of isomorphism) → Inclusive (combines with other elements and becomes higher order)/Falls (dismissed due to contradiction). Record and turn.
Operational flow (divergence → convergence in the shortest distance)
1. divergence (10 minutes)
Drop a small specific memo (1 memo = 1 claim/1 fact).
If in doubt, don't force tagging = put it underdeveloped.
2. light convergence (10 minutes)
Add at least two links to each memo (e.g., related concepts/ counterexamples).
Use line links to clarify "which line and which line resonated" (aiming for critical backlinks).
3. making a nameplate (10 minutes)
Attach headings and one-sentence summaries to adjacent pages (the "faceplates" of the KJ method).
Assign a "state tag" on the spot: 🍼Undeveloped/🧱Stable/🕸Inclusive/🗑Fallen.
Point: Write first, then connect later, then summarize, in this order, and then write a clean copy (one-dimensional book) at the end.
Linking & Tagging Conventions (Mini-Conventions)
Noun for page name (short and unambiguous)/synonym puts a thin page for redirects.
Line link first: Copying and pasting quotations is convenient, but breaks references. Link to the original line whenever possible.
A minimum set of related terms (optional): `is-a / part-of / supports / refutes / example-of` may be written at the beginning of each line (over-labeling is x).
Measure and review (lightweight KPIs)
Isolation rate: Isolated pages divided by total pages (the lower the better).
Average number of backlinks: a measure of convergence (the higher the better).
Critical ratio: percentage of rows with multiple backlinks (the "bud" of convergence).
Number of inclusive events: Number of newly established links between different clusters.
In both cases, it is sufficient to use Scrapbox's list of links for manual measurement → count only monthly.
anti-pattern
Make a huge category table ahead of time/struggle with classification as you write.
Reference cutoff by copying and pasting (erasing evidence of convergence).
Premature clearing (tree fixing) kills the network.
A move right now (in 15 minutes)
Select 5 items from today's notes and add 2 links + status tag to each.
Add a nameplate line (title + one sentence) to the connected islets.
Make sure to create "one across the branch" (i.e., one seed of convergence).
If necessary, this operation can be canvassed into a one-page "Operating Rules" (with sample templates).

An example of an abstract thought that was abstracted to a point where humans could not understand it, but when it was pulled back, it produced an idea that made sense to humans.
Creation to be broken while [connected with the basis].
Changing something changes something that normally stays the same.
Because people don't focus on the things that change from time to time on a regular basis.
For example, the interpretation that "the sun revolves around the earth" has remained unchanged over the years as a worldview shared by many.
This change in "things that don't usually change" is usually considered "[destruction]".
The new worldview that "the earth revolves around the sun" is destroying the traditional worldview.
Breaking is usually viewed negatively.
Many people think that the interpretation that has survived until now is more correct.
However, if the destruction is based on evidence, more people feel that the destruction is right.
This is [creation].

Normally, we think there is a "line" between A and B, but in reality, it is an "event" where we see a new aspect of A because we saw B.
Example: When we look at a friend (A) as a "teacher (B)", the "teaching ability" aspect of the same person suddenly rises.

The interpretation depends on what is considered a single lump.

For example: "How to create concentration" can be seen by dividing "3 months of studying for entrance exams" into chunks, and "Tips for making it a habit" can be seen by dividing it into "1 hour every day".

Even if there is no content yet, if you put an "empty link" of a word you want to connect in the future, it is easy for other information to be gathered there later.

4) "Aliases are not "the same thing" but are combined into "one bundle".

Sometimes the same thing is referred to in different ways (e.g. hay fever = allergic rhinitis). If we bundle them together as "the same group" without forcing them to be mashed into one piece, we can see the difference in the way they say things.
Failure to assume that everything is "the same" will result in throwing out hints that are based on subtle differences.
5) "Importance = not something that comes up often, but something that "bridges the gap."
It is not true that the more often something appears, the more important it is. Rather, it is more important to build "bridges" that connect stories that are far apart and open up new paths.
For example: A "glossary" or "dictionary of people's names" in the workplace is a bridge to leapfrog conversation.

The explanation of the quickest way is useful, but understanding is greatly enhanced when even one alternative path can be found.

"Quotes" that cannot be returned to their original source (vague or unsubstantiated sources) are dangerous.

lines.text: Manipulation of visibility and Sekite, layer, and quotient
[GPT5.icon]
We are talking about three different "[manipulations of visibility]" that can be reused by dropping them into the same mathematical frame.
Correspondence (intuition)
table:_
Manipulation of Reality What Changes? Vessels in the abstract
Change of [way of saying] (expression, translation, change of viewpoint) Change the way A is mapped without touching A itself.
Change [delimiters] (chapters/scope/context) How much of a context is the same as another layer/pre-layer (pasting together each "open set")
Change of [bundling method] (alias/synonymous integration granularity) How far to equate Quotient (divide by equivalence relation / trajectory of group action)
Point:
The three appear to be separate, but are actually all "view conversions".
When put on the instrument (Sekitei/Layer/Quotient), synthesis, comparison, and difference detection can be done with the same moves.
1) Change of wording = Sekite
Example: The same event is referred to in a "technical memo", "summary for management", and "English translation".
Advantages of capturing with the function hand:
Synthesizable (evaluate the order effect of the chain, e.g., specialized -> plain -> summary).
Can say preserved/unpreserved (e.g., keep evidence links but increase ambiguity).
Diversion: research -> public relations, design -> support, education -> exam preparation... the same evaluation axis can be used across expression types.
2) Change of delimitation = layer
E.g., "Talk about the chapter alone/talk about the book as a whole/include related externals".
The advantage of capturing it in layers:
Local-global alignment can be measured ([coordination disorder]`[c]` to detect "correct in part but misaligned in whole").
Boundary operations (opening and closing of ranges) can be reused in other areas.
Diversion: departmental summary ↔ company-wide document, functional unit ↔ whole product, class session ↔ whole semester... common treatment of contextual granularity issues.
3) Change in bundling method = quotient
Examples: Garoon=Garoon=Gr(in-house)" as a bundle/not as a bundle, ICU=Intensive Care Unit or University.
Advantages to be captured in the quotient:
The integration granularity can be continuously adjusted (finely differentiated ↔ roughly integrated).
Breaking the invariants (shortest path, cluster change) before/after the quotient can be treated as "novelty".
Diversion: medical terminology, different notation of laws and regulations, social networking handles and real names... The danger/utility of identification is evaluated with the same tool.
Why is it advantageous to have the "same frame"?
1. order effects (noncommutative) can be handled in a batch
Bundle first and then cut the range (𝔅𝔔) vs. cut the range first and then bundle (𝔔𝔅) with difference = curvature 𝒦.
Even if the domain changes, the method of finding "order difference = novelty" can be used as it is.

pages.title: Equilibrium is determined by the ability to govern the value function.

lines.text: Equilibrium is determined by the ability to govern the value function.
I think you don't understand the context of the answer, but I'm saving it because I feel it's not entirely unhelpful.
next  [When AI removes the constraints of human implementation, it moves to a fast but fragile regime of speculatour dominance.]
[GPT5.icon]
Yes. The equilibrium moves. I'll make a quick rundown with a premise.
Hypothetical mapping
[speculator] = design and selection of hypotheses, meaning making, and preferences (value functions).
[Lancé] = implementation, operation, and validation (launch and iterative improvement).

Under the constraint of human implementation, the two sides complemented each other and a cycle was established due to the difference in cost and speed. When the ranche side is replaced by AI with higher precision and lower cost, the reaction function shifts and the equilibrium point shifts.
What will happen (intuition → design theory)
1. moving bottlenecks

Implementation cost $c_R \to \varepsilon$, thus increasing the throughput of search (speculatour) -> implementation (ranche). The stumbling block is the definition, prioritization, and approval of the value function (= human side).
⇒ The speed of determining value/correctness becomes dominant over the "speed of thinking".
2. shortening of iterations and amplification of externalities
Launch→Learn→Re-Launch is faster, and even small misconfigurations are greatly diffused.
⇒ Auditability, throttling, and sandboxing are essential.
3. diversity vs. convergence tradeoff
While a lower fixed cost of implementation increases the number of concurrent hypotheses, a single evaluation function causes **mode collapse (convergence to a homogeneous solution)**.
⇒ To parallel search + multi-objective optimization (Pareto surface) design.
4. shifting concentration points of power
From execution authority to setting authority for objective functions and constraints.
⇒ Governance shifts the emphasis to a multi-layered agreement on **"what is good**" rather than on "who will execute it.
5. redefining human comparative advantage
AI will be stronger in factual reasoning and implementation. Human dominance will remain in value negotiation, interest adjustment, and legitimization (accountability).
New equilibrium image (proto design)
Thin loop:
Human (value function, boundary conditions) → AI (design, sim, implementation) → Telemetry → AI (factorization) → Human (value update).
Double key:
(1) Objective function key (cannot be changed without human agreement)
(2) Execution key (AI can be executed automatically, but not extraterritorially)
Membrane design:
Sandbox -> staged release -> production. Mandatory testing and explanation of cross-border conditions.
Observability:
Auditable log of all runs (AI decision -> change -> impact). Standardized causal traces that can be reversed.
Distribution and throttling:
Quotas are assigned to each value function and load is internalized through externality taxes.
Indicators (measure of equilibrium moved)
Cycle time (from hypothesis to production reflection)
Search diversity (JSD for concurrent hypotheses, coverage)
Cost of externalities (per unit time for accidents/complaints/compensation)
Explanability ratio (percentage of material changes for which explanations and rationale are available)
Consensus update latency (time required to change value function)
Implementation Steps (Minimum Configuration)
1. decompose value functions: separate objects for objectives, constraints, ethics, and KPIs, and separate change authority.
Declare the automatic promotion rule from Dev→Shadow→Canary→Full. 2.
3. causal log: event log with input→decision→output→effect signature.
4. multi-purpose tuning: having a set of weights, not fixed weights, and selecting them according to the situation.
5. reallocation of human decision points: concentrate on value function updates rather than pre-op.

In short, when AI fills the runche, the cycle does not disappear, but is "lifted to the upper (value/agreement) side and reshaped. The equilibrium will be determined not by the "limits of implementation capability" but by the "governance capability of the value function.

3 rounds of 3

2. collective reflection: interactive exploration and evaluation of Round 1 summary opinions (simple lists are preferred over complex visualizations). ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/we-the-peoples-first-national-conversation-freedom-and-equality-409dedfb02cd])

Scale and Disclosure

2,500+ people from all 435 precincts will be recruited by a third party (Rep Data), aiming for census-aligned representativeness. lines.text: ASDs retain details in memory, non-ASDs summarize.
Exploring the different cognitive, emotional and imaginative experiences of autistic and non-autistic adult readers when contemplating serious literature as compared to non-fiction
https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1001268/full
[GPT5.icon]

Thirteen adults on the autism spectrum ([ASD]) and 13 adults with non-ASD were asked to "read short texts while listening to audio readings" (four literary texts and four nonfiction texts). The results showed that ASD readers tended to identify with the inner life of the characters while retaining "details and ambiguity," and tended to remember the characters "as persons" after reading the texts. Non-ASD readers tend to extract the main points and compress them into a "message. Recorded readings may slow down the reading rhythm to help immersion, but this is different from the effect of live shared reading. [The key to overcoming the "double-empathy problem" is to rethink the design of the live reading.
Research design (rough)
Participants: 7 ASD, 6 non-ASD (adults).
Stimulus: 8 short sentences (3 pages each).
Group A: Subjects related to autism and mutual incompatibility (double empathy) (e.g., Sherlock, Eleanor Oliphant, Uta Frith interview, Chris Packham article)
Group B: More general human disadvantages and emotions (e.g. Great Expectations, essays, etc.)
Procedure: listen to the audio reading → reflective questionnaire for each text → follow-up interview (reread excerpts and reimmersion).
Analysis: literal close reading + thematic analysis.
Major Findings
1. reading transition: Surface → Intuitive immersion
Fiction** gives "room for imagination by not telling the story, "** and immersion occurs because of sudden "moving emotions.
Non-fiction (commentary style) **"teach/tell "** comes to the fore, and imaginative empathy is difficult to generate.
Imaginative Feeling

ASD Readers: express themselves with musical metaphors** (in tune / rang true, etc.) that are **"attunement" with the characters and text. Naturally moves back and forth between reevaluating one's own past experiences and observing oneself from a third person's point of view. Easy to maintain multiple perspectives of a person or scene at the same time.
Non-ASD readers: tend to flow into the application of normative/procedural empathy, "you should empathize with ~," and conclude before getting inside the person.
[Normative empathy]/[Procedural empathy]
3. retention and utilization after reading
ASD: The person itself (per complexity) can be kept in mind and used later to reinterpret specific social situations.
Non-ASD: data compressed and retained as core messages and lessons learned (easier to generalize, but reduces complexity).
[nishio.icon]
[AI Summary] has a common structure with uninteresting problems.
When we had this discussion, we talked about how AI summaries are uninteresting because they throw out all the branches and leaves and just use abstract descriptions.
[Story intersections become atoms.] In [Associative connection of branches and leaves] we talked.
ASD is able to discover atoms because it retains the experience stories of others as stories
4. implications for theory

The authors reject the simplistic model that "autism is a lack of empathy," and suggest that ASD is a highly empathetic person with details and ambiguity, and that social "spaciousness" is not impaired.
On the other hand, **differences in cognitive style (detail retention vs. summary compression) can contribute to mutual misunderstanding (double empathy)**.
5. design of reading/pre-reading
Recorded reading: while it reduces speed reading and aids immersion, the surprise and interaction of live-ability is weak.
Live co-reading (existing research): Possibly effective in promoting mutual understanding between different neurotypes. Suggestion to consider less burdensome formats such as live online.
Practical Implications
If you want to create a place that goes beyond double-empathy:
Start with fiction, especially contemporary literature that includes "difficulties and discrepancies" (classics can be easily superimposed due to anxiety about "reading" them correctly).
Live (or pseudo-live) readings + small-group dialogues are designed to explore the "unsaid parts" together.

Thoughts should be **"What did you perceive (the tremor in the person)?", then "Why did you feel that way (the words of the text)?", then "From a different perspective?" **If you deepen in the order of **, retention (as a person)** is more likely to occur than compression.
limit
Sample small/highly educated bias, positive reading demographics. The demographic in need of reading support has not yet been examined.
The effect of live co-reading was not directly tested with recorded readings only.
Long-term transition to the real world has not yet been evaluated.
in a word

Literature trains us to live with the "complexity in the other person," with ASD having a strong "power to hold complexity" and non-ASD having a strong "power to summarize. The key to going beyond double empathy is to have a "near-live, collaborative reading space" where the strengths of both can meet."

[ASD is not a lack of empathy.]

Add "nation" and "model" to the triangle.
prev:  [Markets, Hierarchies, and Communities]
[GPT5.icon]
Copy. Based on the premise of the triangle (market, hierarchy, and community), the pentagonal model as an "extended" version of the triangle will be explained in a compact manner.
What is the Pentagonal Model?

A framework designed on the premise that five "forces" are simultaneously deployed and interfere with each other by adding **State (State) and Model (AI, Algorithm, Platform)** to the three coordination principles.
Market: Diversification adjustment with price signals
Hierarchy: Centralized coordination with orders and plans
Community: autonomous adjustment by norms and reputation
State: coordination with enforcement in laws, regulations, supervision, and public procurement
Model: Implement "invisible planning" with recommendations, search rankings, dynamic pricing, etc.
Why we need two additional poles (one per line)
State: Standards, certifications, subsidies, and sanctions were the main causes of the simultaneous rearrangement of supply networks.
Model: platform algo permanently reallocates demand, exposure, and labor allocation (quasi-planned economy).
(omitted)
Rearrangement of positioning (triangle -> pentagon)
The triangle is still the core. However, states and models are treated as operable levers, not "exogenous environments.
Result: Clear delineation of responsibility and avoiding misinterpretation of policy/algo changes as "market whims".
Outcome: adaptability during normal times + resilience during disturbances can be maximized at the same time.
super-summary
Add the state and model to the triangle and design and monitor five adjustment levers simultaneously.
Measures will be evaluated on three layers of information x logistics x energy, switching between the two phases of peacetime/disturbance.
This allows on-demand diversity peer production to operate as a complementary cycle.
**The "necessity "** of adding "state" and "model" to the triangle is explained in detail, not in a single line (avoiding implementation theory and concentrating on concepts and phenomena).
1) Why make "State" an independent pole?
(a) Qualitatively different adjustment mechanisms
The state redefines the space of action itself with coercive power (law, licensing, sanctions, taxation, subsidies), whereas market = price, hierarchy = command, community = norm.
The state can change the **boundary conditions (what is allowed/required)** that prices and internal orders are "given" from a higher level.
(b) The range and simultaneity of effects are orders of magnitude greater

Simultaneity: Carbon taxes, medical and construction certifications, import/export regulations, infrastructure fees, etc. will be applied simultaneously to all players, rearranging the supply chain all at once.
Cross-border: tariffs, embargoes, and data cross-border regulations move borders that companies and communities cannot move.
(c) In triangles, the explanation escapes to "exogenous shocks".

For example, even if the market structure shifts in the case of public procurement (a huge demand of the state), the triangular shape of the market would be simply "the market has changed," and the state as an "operable lever" would not be visible.
As a result, policy-induced changes are misinterpreted as price changes, resulting in erroneous learning and optimization.
(d) Response to counterexample.
Response: "State intervention can be internalized in prices (fines = costs)."
→ Fines are only partially applied. The core is **"non-priceable" restrictions** such as entry bans, business suspensions, confiscation, criminal penalties, etc.
Response: "Regulation is a corporate lobby, a de facto market."
→ The existence of lobbying activities is not denied, but only the state has the power to enforce final decisions.
2) Why make "Model (Model: AI, Algorithm, Platform)" an independent pole?
(a) The medium of adjustment is "neither price nor command nor norm."
Algorithmic interventions such as exposure, recommendations, search rankings, matching, rate limiting, dynamic pricing, etc., permanently redistribute demand, labor, and information flows.
This functions as a quasi-plan because it precedes and runs parallel to prices (the market) and forms the front end of the decision-making process.
(b) Minor design changes spill over into huge real economy

One coefficient of recommendation, one throttle threshold of API, and sales, visibility, participation rates, and travel demand are transferred on a large scale ("gatekeeping" nature of the platform economy).
Moreover, changes are high frequency and private, which differs from the transparent decision-making process of hierarchy and community.
(c) Reasons why inclusions into triangles fail.
If we reduce it to "part of the market (ad prices)" or "part of the company's internal orders (product decisions)," we cannot see which "algo intervention" is the main body of causation.
Exposure/recommendation is often a zero sum allocation problem (if you raise someone, someone else will go down). Prices and norms alone cannot describe it.
(d) Response to counterexample.
Counterargument: "Algos can operate under community norms (OSS-ization)."
→ Possible, but most of them are black boxes of private companies. And even with OSS, if data and distribution rules are managed separately, they remain as independent poles.
Response: "The model is a tool of corporate "hierarchy
→ A social lever that goes beyond the usual hierarchical imperative in that it continuously reallocates the action space of external players, even if the decision is made within a company.
3) Advantages (theoretical and practical) of considering the two as "independent poles
(Theory) Increased explanatory power
We can separate and model the causality of policy shock-driven rearrangements (tariffs, certifications, subsidies) and algo-driven rearrangements (exposure, search, fees).
Phenomena that tend to be pushed out as "exogenous variables" in triangles can be treated as endogenous levers.
(Practice) Liability Boundary and Observability
The "whose levers moved what" can be tracked in the **Change History (Official Gazette and Release Notes)**.
Reproducible verification of policy and algo changes without confusing them with "market whims" (A/B Impact Assessment).
(Risk) Address heterogeneity of failure modes
State: excess, delay, arbitrariness / Model: opacity, bias, runaway - risks of a different system than market, hierarchy, community.
By separating the poles, the audit and remediation design can be tailored to each.
4) How far is a "state/model" and how far is a triangle (boundary conditions)?
When the state pole is weakened: In less effective laws (failed states), markets, hierarchies, and communities are relatively led.
If the model pole is thin: If fully transparent recommendations, public APIs, collaborative governance, and data commons are established, the model pole can be absorbed by the community pole.
Criteria for practical decisions:
1. enforceability (non-price penalty for non-compliance)
2. control of front-end allocation (who decides what is "visible/encounterable/usable")
3. simultaneity, frequency, and transparency of changes
summary
The state is the higher mechanism that forcibly rewrites the "premise" of prices and orders,
The model is a quasi-planning mechanism that constantly reallocates the "front end" of decision-making,

Therefore, it is reasonable to set up the two as independent poles, rather than encompassing them in a triangle, in terms of explanatory power of the phenomenon, delimitation of responsibility, and risk design.

**The idea of treating the state and the model (algorithm/platform)** as independent poles, based on the triangle (market, hierarchy, community), is a "junction" of the classics below and recent "platform/algorithm governance" research.
Triangular base

Formulation of market x hierarchy boundaries: Coase (1937)/Williamson (1975). Explained by the use of "orders and plans" and market transactions within firms = transaction costs. ([rochelleterman.com https://rochelleterman.com/ir/sites/default/files/Coase%201937.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Third form (network/community): Powell (1990) presents a network organization that is "neither market nor hierarchical"; Ostrom (1990) demonstrates autonomous governance of the commons; Powell (1990) presents a network organization that is "neither market nor hierarchical"; Ostrom (1990) demonstrates autonomous governance of the commons. ([Stanford University https://web.stanford.edu/~woodyp/powell_neither.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Basis for considering the "State" as an independent pole.

A "higher-level mechanism" that simultaneously reconfigures the assumptions of the behavioral space through legal enforcement, such as regulations, certifications, tariffs, and public procurement. See also Williamson's review and retrospect. ([Stanford Graduate School of Business, https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/books/firms-markets-hierarchies-transaction-cost-economics- perspective?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Basis for considering "model (algo/PF)" as an independent pole

[Code is Law: [Lessig] argues that architecture (code) is the "fourth regulation" that regulates behavior. A regulating medium different from prices, commands, and norms. ([harvardmagazine.com https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2000/01/code-is-law-html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

[Algorithmic governance]/regulation: [Yeung (2018)] theorizes "[algorithmic regulation]" in which recommendation, scoring, dynamic pricing, etc., continuously modify behavior. ([Wiley Online Library https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/rego.12158?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

[platform governance]: Gillespie (2018) describes "gatekeeping" where moderation and exposure design redistribute the public sphere; Van Dijck/Poell/de Waal (2018) provides a comprehensive overview of social infrastructuring as a tripartite market, government, platform Pasquale (2015) and Zuboff (2019) analyze empowerment as [black-boxing] and [surveillance capitalism]. ([Yale University Press https://yalebooks.yale.edu/book/9780300261431/custodians-of-the-internet/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
placement
With the above classics (Coase/Williamson/Powell/Ostrom), the frame of the triangle is established,
The Lessig/Yeung/Gillespie/Van Dijck lineage demonstrated "algo-distribution "**, which is neither price, command, nor norm, and its social range.

Furthermore, if we stand independently of simultaneous simultaneous reallocations due to state coercion, we can endogenously model policy-induced and algo-induced reallocations - this is the academic underpinning of the pentopole model.

pages.title: Considerably Improving Clustering Algorithms Using UMAP Dimensionality Reduction Technique: A Comparative Study

lines.text: Considerably Improving Clustering Algorithms Using UMAP Dimensionality Reduction Technique: A Comparative Study
A study that "dimensionality reduction with UMAP followed by clustering greatly improves accuracy and computation time."
Considerably Improving Clustering Algorithms Using UMAP Dimensionality Reduction Technique: A Comparative Study
[Allaoui et al. 2020]
[PDF https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/978-3-030-51935-3_34.pdf]
[https://gyazo.com/47a4ecc636b7a8303f7a26e9178fcb4e]
[GPT5.icon]
Main Points (Conclusion)

Both accuracy (Accuracy/NMI) and execution time are improved when high-dimensional data is embedded in lower dimensions with UMAP and then K-means/GMM/agglomerative hierarchies/HDBSCAN is applied. In many cases, GMM and hierarchical systems in particular show significant improvement. ([ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340388772_Considerably_Improving_Clustering_Algorithms_Using_UMAP_ Dimensionality_Reduction_Technique_A_Comparative_Study?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

The subject is 5 image-based datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, UMIST Faces, PenDigits, and USPS). ([ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340388772_Considerably_Improving_Clustering_Algorithms_Using_UMAP_ Dimensionality_Reduction_Technique_A_Comparative_Study?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Contents of Experiment

Comparison algorithm: K-means/GMM/Aglomerative/HDBSCAN run in original feature space vs. embedded space after UMAP and compared. Evaluated by Accuracy and NMI.([ACM Digital Library https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1007/978-3-030-51935-3_34?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Example results (from the table in the paper):

K-means（MNIST）：Accuracy 0.53 → 0.91、NMI 0.48 → 0.85。([ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340388772_Considerably_Improving_Clustering_Algorithms_Using_UMAP_Dimensionality_Reduction_Technique_A_Comparative_Study?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

K-means（UMIST Faces）：0.43 → 0.74。([ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340388772_Considerably_Improving_Clustering_Algorithms_Using_UMAP_Dimensionality_Reduction_Technique_A_Comparative_Study?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Agglomerative（USPS）：0.68 → 0.96。([ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340388772_Considerably_Improving_Clustering_Algorithms_Using_UMAP_Dimensionality_Reduction_Technique_A_Comparative_Study?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

GMM described an improvement of over 34% in Accuracy and 25% in NMI in 3 out of 5 data. ([ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340388772_Considerably_Improving_Clustering_Algorithms_Using_UMAP_ Dimensionality_Reduction_Technique_A_Comparative_Study?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Computation time: HDBSCAN is over 26 minutes (in original space) → reduced to about 5 seconds (MNIST/F-MNIST) after UMAP. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7340901/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
How it should be interpreted (practical implications)

UMAP→Clustering" is a promising pretreatment: it is easy to increase separability and computational efficiency when clusters are entangled or have many unwanted dimensions. Subsequent studies and surveys support this policy. ([SpringerLink https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10618-023-00980-2?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

The UMAP author's document also warns that "there are some arguments. For clustering purposes, it is recommended to use 10 to 50 dimensions for embedding, not just 2D, and then run HDBSCAN, etc. on them. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/clustering.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Guideline for Hyperpara:
`n_neighbors` is a local/global tradeoff (smaller is local, closer to cluster).
`min_dist` is smaller (0-0.3 approx) if you want to tighten the cluster. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/parameters.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Other domains such as text: some experiments in document clustering report that clustering is stable when dropped to 15 or more dimensions in UMAP and then clustered, and that the effect of tuning is limited. ([ACL Antology https://aclanthology.org/2023.nejlt-1.7.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Limitations / Caution

Target is centered on 5 image-based datasets, generalization to other domains needs to be verified. ([ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340388772_Considerably_Improving_Clustering_Algorithms_Using_UMAP_ Dimensionality_Reduction_Technique_A_Comparative_Study?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Since dimensionality reduction may distort the neighborhood relationship, it is safe to compare the cluster results with the cluster results in the original space while checking the embedding quality with trustworthiness, etc. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/clustering.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If necessary, I can organize the numbers in this paper a bit more and provide a table of "what worked for which algorithm x data".
[nishio.icon]
This study [BERTopic: Neural topic modeling with a class-based TF-IDF] is mentioned as justification for UMAP

However, since the dataset is entirely image-based and there is a strong correlation between the axes, it is difficult to say whether it would behave in the same way in a natural language [Clustering after UMAP of embedded vectors] situation.
And then I thought, there was a study that showed that clustering after UMAP in 2 dimensions is less accurate.
[An Empirical Configuration Study of a Common Document Clustering Pipeline]
In other words, the data in the image-based data set would have been less susceptible to the disadvantages of dimensionality reduction by being distributed around low-dimensional manifolds.
[Document embedding using UMAP — umap 0.5.8 documentation https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/document_embedding.html]

The performance tends to reach a ceiling at 10-15 dimensions, and extremely low dimensions such as 2D are disadvantageous. On the time side, measurements show that UMAP's computational cost strongly depends on `n_neighbors` (20 to a few seconds, 1280 to several hundred seconds).
Dropping to two dimensions is obviously a bad idea.[nishio.icon]
Documentation for [UMAP]: Document Embedding Tutorial

20 The flow of text embedding -> UMAP -> HDBSCAN was introduced on the subject of Newsgroups (labeled text), confirming that documents on the same topic can be grouped into neighborhoods. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/document_embedding.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
This is not an embedded vector.[TfidfVectorizer]だね[nishio.icon]
Design intent of [BERTopic]/[Top2Vec] system

BERTopic is based on the premise of "embedding → UMAP → HDBSCAN → c-TF-IDF," and Top2Vec also has "UMAP to reduce dimension → HDBSCAN to detect high-density regions" at its core. Top2Vec also has a core concept of "reduce dimension with UMAP → detect high-density regions with HDBSCAN" and compensates for the distortion of UMAP by computing topic vectors in the original high-dimensional space ("UMAP+HDBSCAN is a 'labeling process' and the topic representative vector calculation is performed in the original space"). ([maartengr.github.io https://maartengr.github.io/BERTopic/getting_started/dim_reduction/dim_reduction.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com ])
Relevance of the dimensionality reduction itself (text)

The LREC 2024 evaluation study reported that a dimensionality reduction of about 50% by sentence-embedded PCA resulted in little performance degradation and in fact improved performance in some cases. Even if not limited to non-linear UMAPs, the study shows that **"moderately reduce "** is more reasonable than "keep high dimensionality" in many cases. ([ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2024.lrec-main.579.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
This is irrelevant to "what happens when you drop it into 2D" because it is only a reduction of at most 50%.[nishio.icon]
2) Why does it work in text (geometry perspective)?
Cosine Geometry and Neighborhood Conservation

The sentence embedding is conventionally L2-normalized and treated as a cosine distance; UMAP can construct a neighborhood graph at arbitrary distances (such as `metric='cosine'`) and map it to a lower dimension while preserving the neighborhood structure. The general design is to run k-means/HDBSCAN at the Euclid distance to the coordinates thus obtained. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/document_embedding.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Anisotropy" in BERT systems

Sentence embedding space tends to concentrate on narrow cones = distance tends to lose its discriminative power. It has been reported that geometry alignment through preprocessing such as normalization and whitening improves cluster separation, one reason why it works well with UMAP preprocessing. ([ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/D19-1006/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3) However: UMAP pretreatment precautions
Density is not fully preserved → HDBSCAN decisions can change

UMAP preserves "neighborhoods" but the density is easily distorted, which can cause HDBSCAN to oversplit/overjoin. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/clustering.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Reproducibility (randomness, data order dependence)

UMAP is stochastic. Reproducibility can be increased by fixing `random_state`, but it is not perfect, and even input order and parallelization can make a difference (BERTopic FAQ/UMAP reproducibility explanation and Issue). ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reproducibility.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
calculation cost
As `n_neighbors` is increased, UMAP computation time increases rapidly (measured figures are available), and some experiments have shown that it is reasonable to stop around 10-15 dimensions.
4) Guideline in practice (assuming text embedding)
A. Parallel baselines (try both first)
1. direct clustering: HDBSCAN (`metric='cosine'`) directly into the original embedding.
Linear reduction: Reduce to 50-200 dimensions with PCA, then HDBSCAN/k-means.
3. umap reduction: umap (starting from `metric='cosine'`, `n_components=10-15`, `min_dist∈[0,0.3]`, `n_neighbors=15-50`) → HDBSCAN/k -means.
Comparisons are made with ARI/AMI (with labels) or Silhouette/DBI + topic coherence (e.g. c_v) + **stability (re-training agreement at bootstrap)**.
B. Initial value of Hypara
UMAP: `metric='cosine'`, `n_components=10-15` and `n_neighbors≈20` are textbook initial points. The larger `n_neighbors` is, the heavier the computation becomes.

HDBSCAN: `min_cluster_size` is the size you want the cluster to be at least this large. Allocation to all points can be done by `soft_clustering` (probability output) if necessary. ([hdbscan.readthedocs.io https://hdbscan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/basic_hdbscan.html])
C. When to Avoid/Refrain from UMAP
Cluster boundary stability is paramount (auditability is critical)

Density distortion is critical (e.g., want to treat differences in frequency of occurrence as densities as they are) → Consider density preserving versions such as densMAP. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/densmap_demo.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If the data is small and the original dimensions (e.g., 384/768 dimensions) are sufficient for HDBSCAN to work.
First, when a PCA-based lightweight system is sufficient. ([ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2024.lrec-main.579.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
D. If you use UMAP

Suppress the effect of random selection: fix `random_state`, run several times with the same conditions and see the match rate. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reproducibility.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Reported that L2 normalization (at least after UMAP) makes it easier to stabilize.

Following Top2Vec, it is also useful to use UMAP space for labeling and original space for computing representative vectors and centroids. ([ar5iv https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2008.09470?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
summary

Multiple studies and implementations have shown that UMAP preprocessing is beneficial in terms of both quality and computation (with appropriate dimensions and parameters) not only for images but also for text embedding. HDBSCAN/k-means is a strong composition, especially when reduced to 10-15 dimensions.

On the other hand, because of the tradeoff of density distortion/reproducibility, it is safe to run alongside the baseline without UMAP/with PCA and choose based on external indicators (ARI/AMI), internal indicators, topic coherence, and stability. ([umap-learn.readthedocs.io https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/clustering.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If necessary, prepare a **minimum experimental design (table of indicators + recommended hyperlaparas & code fragments)** that can be turned directly into A-D above for the corpus at hand.

An Empirical Configuration Study of a Common Document Clustering Pipeline
Study shows that clustering after dropping to 2 dimensions in UMAP reduces accuracy.

Case Analysis from the Gendlin Perspective (Focusing Perspective)
summary

This dialogue is able to handle the client's words with clean-language-style repetitive questions, but does not fully access the felt sense of the body (vague but holistic) that is at the core of Gendlin's Focusing. As a result, the tension of "I have to do it" is returning to the thought process of "clarify how to do it," and I have the impression that the felt shift (one step lighter change at the body level) has not fully occurred.
