What works well
Reflection of client language: metaphors (i.e., candidate handles) such as "wall," "engine," "drive force," and "energy" came naturally.
Clarification of the action subject: The value of wanting to make decisions on one's own/not being easily burned by tasks given from the outside was expressed.
Visualization of the process: the choice of parallel projects was symbolized as a "barrier to progress".
stumbling
Lack of guidance to the body: "Where is it?" What kind?" are more likely to lean toward conceptual definitions, and **checking with the body (resonance)** is less likely to occur.
Lack of pacing: there is no margin for pause and silence, and time is not taken to listen inwardly.
Handling the "I don't know": "What do you think?" and reinforced the "it should be solved" argument.
I thought this.[nishio.icon]
I'm biased to only ask questions about the last statement, and I'm not grasping what's still not clear.
Quickness of Targeting: Early return to the problem-solution loop of "identify the solution". Lack of support to stay on the edge (borderline between know/not know).
If you want to do it in a focusing way (short protocol: walking version 5-7 minutes)
1. place attention on the soles of the feet and breathing
One deep breath in step. Make the "here and now" in your body.
2. feel the whole

Search for the "overall feeling of 'I must do it'" with the body (chest, throat, abdomen, shoulders, etc.). Do not try to put it into words, but capture it in terms of texture (heaviness/rushes/pressure/temperature).
3. find the handle
Try to guess the perfect word/image that fits the whole now (e.g., "wall," "blockage," "fog"). Check the fit with your body (resonance).
4. ask at the edge
What is the smallest thing this wall wants from me right now?
Wait for a small "thump" to come from the body (a physical step that can be done in 10 minutes is preferable).
5. receive
Felt shift if there is a slight change (breathing passes/strength is lost, etc.). Respect and note the step that came out.
Examples of question substitution that make use of metaphors
×x "Where is it?"
→ "Where on your body do you feel it most?" (If not, "What texture as a whole?")
×x "What type of drive force?"
→ How does your body react when you get one step closer to that "engine/wall"?
×x "If you could do that, what would you do?"
→ What is the smallest step your body says you need to take now for the "wall" to soften a bit?
Resonance check: "Does that word (e.g., 'easy to break') fit when you apply it to your body/is it any different?"
Using Focusing to Select Parallel Projects (10 minute algorithm)
1. call to mind (in order) up to three candidate project names.
2. observe the body's response to each project name (breathing/shoulders/looseness/clogging in the groin).
3.**Select the one that is the most "breathable/lightest "**.
4. ask the body for the **"next step (10 minutes)** of the project (e.g., inventory one item on the list, open the relevant folder, ping the person in charge with one line, etc.).
5. commit to perform (timer 10 minutes). When you finish, check the degree of fit with your body again.
Operational checklist on the therapist's side
□ Observe the rhythm of reflection → silence → return to the body
Why? From ** "What is the body now?" **
□ Respect "I don't know" (= sign that you have reached the edge)
→Let's feel the whole "unknowability" together.
□ Welcome a step too small (carry forward rather than cognitive resolution)
Improvement Dialog (short example)
Visitor: "A wall is standing in my way."
Supporter: "Let's see how the whole "wall" feels with your body now. ...... (wait a little). Where do you feel it the most?"
Visitor: "My chest area is hard."
Supporter: "Is 'wall' the right word for that firmness, or is it a little different?"
Interviewee: "'thick board' is closer."
Supporter: "Ask your ...... body what one step you can take in 10 minutes that is needed now for a "thicker board."
Visitor: "Don't list all the projects, just open one memo on Project A first."
Supporter: "So what happens to the firmness of the chest at one level?"
summary
Currently, it is easy to return to thinking with repetitive meta-questions, and the flow of felt sense to felt shift is weak.

Metaphors ([wall] / [engine] / [energy]) are good handles. Between the confirmation of resonance with the body and the receipt of the smallest step, it is easy for a natural focus - carry forward to advance to occur.
Next time you try "Walking Focusing 5 minutes" + "1 action for 10 minutes", you can expect a qualitative shift from **"I have to" to "I can "**.

pages.title: What is Provider in the context of Ostrom?

lines.text: What is Provider in the context of Ostrom?
[GPT5.icon]

In short, the "[Provider]" in [Ostrom] is the one who decides "how to provide" resources and public services. Specifically, they are responsible for making decisions on what and how much to provide, procuring funds, arranging production (whether self-managed or outsourced), and monitoring production. ([International Journal of the Commons https://thecommonsjournal.org/articles/10.18352/ijc.904])
Provision ≠ Production

The distinction is that the Provider is the entity that makes the decision to provide the service and arranges for financial resources and contracts, while the Producer is the entity that actually creates/operates the service.
typical example
Waterway: General meeting or board of directors of the water users' association = Provider; construction team or contractor = Producer; each farmer = Appropriator (resource taker).
Fisheries: Fisheries Cooperative (decides the framework for quotas and patrols and collects funds) = Provider, actual operation of buoy placement and patrols = Producer, fishermen = Appropriator.
role overlap
In a self-managed commons, the user (Proprietor) is also the Provider through the association, and sometimes also the Producer through their own work (the actors often overlap).
Relationship to Design Principles

The Provider is responsible for designing and operating the system to achieve this alignment. ([patternsofcommoning.org https://patternsofcommoning.org/uncategorized/eight-design-principles-for-successful-commons/?utm_source= chatgpt.com])

In short, Provider = "governance entity" that "manages provision," Producer = "operational entity" that "creates and operates," and Appropriator = "user entity" that "uses (or draws out). Producer = "actual working entity" that "creates and manages"; Appropriator = "user" that "uses (extracts)". ([International Journal of the Commons https://thecommonsjournal.org/articles/10.18352/ijc.904])

It's confusing, isn't it?

Olson
[GPT5.icon]
Key Points in [Manker Olson], [The Logic of Collective Action] (1965).

When you create [public goods (i.e. goods or services such as parks or highways)] (non-exclusionary and non-competitive) that work for everyone, [reasonable individuals] will [free ride (e.g. on train)], so unless there is a special trick, collective benefits is unlikely to be provided unless there is a special mechanism.
How it works (why does it happen?)
Benefit dilution: If the total benefit of a public good is B for a group of n participants, each person's share is approximately B/n.
2. cost non-dilution: contribution cost c is borne entirely by each person.
3. rational calculation: B/n < c in many situations → it is better not to produce → everyone looks at it → insufficient supply.
Three classifications of groups ([Olson's "Law of Large Groups"])
Privileged group: a small portion gets large benefits (or wealth) and is put out alone. → Easily supplied.
Intermediate group: a scale where they can see each other's actions and where mutual monitoring and negotiation are effective. → Supply with conditions.
Potential group (large scale): the impact of one person's contribution is minimal and free ride is the norm. → Not supplied as is.
Solution (Olson's emphasis)
Selective incentives = "private" quid pro quo (or punishment) that only the contributor gets
Positive incentives: members-only services, honor/reputation, professional network, insurance, limited tools, etc.
Negative incentives: dues obligations, penalties, closed stores (you have to be a union member to work there), etc.
Compulsory: contributions are made obligatory through taxation and legal regulations (state-like powers).
Small grouping: cellularize/federate large herds to increase visibility and mutuality.
Boosting a critical few: "privileged" entities (patrons, leaders) who enjoy many of the benefits shoulder the initial supply and broaden the base.
Visualization of results: shortly show the cause and effect of the contribution→result and make it personalized.
Differences from Hardin (1968) and [prisoner's dilemma
Hardin ([Tragedy of the Commons]): overuse of shared resources (competing resources).
Olson: "Insufficient supply" of public goods (non-competition/non-exclusion).
Prisoner's dilemma: a metaphor for a two-person game; Olson's theory includes even n-person and organizational costs.
concrete example
Labor unions and trade associations: dues = negative incentives; membership benefits = positive incentives.
[open source (software, etc.)]: many are free riders, but a small strong core is [private gain] driven by [reputation]/[employment opportunities].
GPT5, you understand it well.[nishio.icon]
Climate change, public safety, standardization: large scale hence potential grouping → Taxation, regulation, subsidies and club goods are key.
Implications for digital participation design (application perspective)
Design for "free ride": embed selective incentives such as visibility, medals/titles, limited channels, prior access, etc. from the beginning.
Cellularization x Collaboration: National scale operates as a set of local sub-groups, ensuring local and mutuality.
Initial Patronage: Designed for a critical few to "take the first loss" (endowment, matching, bounty).
Outcome short-circuit: shorter lead time from contribution to decision-making and implementation, and increased efficacy.
Points that are often misunderstood
The point is not that "people are altruistic, so it's okay," but that it's hard to sustain without institutional design.

The findings of [ostrom] (1990) provide the conditions for self-management, and in some cases they overturn Olson's pessimism, but in the end, "tricks" such as visualization, sanctions, and agreed-upon rules are the key.

pages.title: Mistakenly identified as Singapore by NURO Optical

lines.text: Mistakenly identified as Singapore by NURO Optical
[GPT5.icon]
Copy that. Let's get to the point first...

Cases in which accesses from Japan are misidentified as "access from Singapore (SG)" due to a combination of some lines and settings have actually occurred. There are three major causes: (1) errors/outdated GeoIP database, (2) routing changes on the terminal side (VPN, Apple Private Relay, etc. relay bases are SG), and (3) misuse of "apparent location" that depends on DNS/Anycast design. ISPs in Japan, including NURO (So-net), have historically experienced (1), and (2) and (3) can occur "regardless of the provider".
Example (Japan → SG misidentification)

Google Search reports "Singapore results" even though from Japan (Official Google Community), suspected case of GeoIP linkage error. ([Google Help https://support.google.com/websearch/thread/90022542/%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E3%81%8B%E3%82%89%E3%81%AE%E3%82%A2%E3%82%AF%E3 %82%BB%E3%82%B9%E3%81%AA%E3%81%AE%E3%81%AB%E3%82%B7%E3%83%B3%E3%82%AC%E3%83%9D%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB%E3%81%AE%E6%A4%9C%E7%B4%A2%E7%B5 90%E6%9E%9C%E3%81%8C%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E3%81%95%E3%82%8C%E3%82%8B?hl=en&utm_source=chatgpt.com])

ABEMA and other distribution services strongly block foreign IPs, so even if you are in Japan, you will not be able to watch if you are "judged as foreign". General guidance on misjudgment. ([ABEMA Help https://help.abema.tv/hc/ja/articles/360020191131--AbemaTV-is-only-accessible-within-Japan-%E3%81%A8%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E 3%81%95%E3%82%8C%E3%81%BE%E3%81%99?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

NURO Hikari: Officials explained that they do not assign overseas IPs, but they acquire and operate IPs that were used overseas in the past by registering them in Japan, and an old GeoIP may result in an overseas judgment. Contact the service provider via support for a response. ([NURO Hikari https://www.nuro.jp/article/kaigai-ip/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Press/Technical commentary: One ISP reused "originally German IP block" and judged overseas with old GeoIP data -> delivery was suspended. **The cause was clearly stated as old GeoIP (especially GeoLite update was stopped)**. The mechanism is the same type for SG misidentification. ([hbol.jp https://hbol.jp/201099/2?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Terminal-side factor: Apple Private Relay's "egress" is internationally distributed (SG partition in the public list). Depending on the settings, the egress may be a neighboring country, causing the service side to make a mistake in determining the country. ([Apple Support https://support.apple.com/ja-jp/102602?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Data saver/VPN/security relay for mobile and browser functions via overseas bases -> general theory that appears to be "overseas IP" (explanation by domestic carriers). ([NTT Docomo SSW https://nttdocomo-ssw.com/nssw/dhkr/ouchinetpress/communication/article458/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Isolation of technical causes
1. inconsistency of GeoIP data

MaxMind handles "registered country" and "actual location" separately. However, old data and erroneous registration can occur. Official contact point for correction is also available. ([support.maxmind.com https://support.maxmind.com/knowledge-base/articles/maxmind-ip-geolocation-data?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2. change of "exit" at terminal side (provider-independent)

▪ Apple Private Relay/VPN/Some browsers data saving feature; Private Relay exit IP range includes SG, and changing the location retention setting may result in exit to a neighboring country. ([mask-api.icloud.com https://mask-api.icloud.com/egress-ip-ranges.csv?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. due to DNS/Anycast

If a site misuses DNS resolver location or anycast termination instead of "client IP" for location estimation, it may be determined that SG PoP has been stepped on (poor design). The existence of APAC PoP operation such as Cloudflare is important as a prerequisite. ([The Cloudflare Blog https://blog.cloudflare.com/ja-jp/connection-errors-in-asia-pacific-region-on-july-9-2023/?utm_source=chatgpt. com])
Issues specific to NURO (So-net)

NURO official: "We do not assign overseas IPs. However, IPs used overseas in the past are operated in Japan, and there are "rare" cases of misjudgment caused by old GeoIPs. NURO can contact the service provider when this occurs. ([NURO Hikari https://www.nuro.jp/article/kaigai-ip/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Historically, several cases of "misclassification as overseas (e.g., Germany)" have been reported. "SG misidentification" can be reproduced by the same mechanism (reassigned IP x old DB) or (2) and (3). ([hbol.jp https://hbol.jp/201099/2?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Diagnostic procedures that can be tried now (in order of reproducibility)
Check your "Viewed IP/ASN

Check MaxMind Demo / DB-IP / IP2Location etc. in order in a browser. If there is a difference, GeoIP inconsistency is high. ([maxmind.com https://www.maxmind.com/en/geoip-demo?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2. disable Private Relay / VPN / data saving (Safari or device settings) -> recheck. ([Apple Support https://support.apple.com/ja-jp/102022?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

3. compare the difference in behavior by switching DNS (ISP's standard DNS ↔ 8.8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1 etc.). isolate Anycast misuse. ([The Cloudflare Blog https://blog.cloudflare.com/ja-jp/connection-errors-in-asia-pacific-region-on-july-9-2023/?utm_source=chatgpt. com])
4. switch IPv4/IPv6 (router setting/temporarily disabled) to see the difference.

5. check the help on the site you are using (e.g. ABEMA/Netflix's region determination rules) ([ABEMA Help https://help.abema.tv/hc/ja/articles/360020191131--AbemaTV-is-only-accessible- within-Japan-%E3%81%A8%E8%A1%A8%E7%A4%BA%E3%81%95%E3%82%8C%E3%81%BE%E3%81%99?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Coping (in order of priority)
Elimination of terminal-side factors: Private Relay/VPN/Data Saver OFF, browser extension proxy function OFF.([Apple Support https://support.apple.com/ja-jp/102602?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Restore DNS to ISP standard (or conversely, change to public DNS) -> Hypothesis testing of design deficiencies with or without improvement. ([The Cloudflare Blog https://blog.cloudflare.com/ja-jp/connection-errors-in-asia-pacific-region-on-july-9-2023/?utm_source=chatgpt. com])

Contact ISP support of NURO, etc.: It has been officially announced that "the operator will request the content side" to correct the problem. ([NURO Hikari https://www.nuro.jp/article/kaigai-ip/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Application for GeoIP correction (to MaxMind, etc.): Application for correction in units of IP/prefix of wrong location. There is a time lag until the result is reflected. ([maxmind.com https://www.maxmind.com/en/geoip-data-correction-request?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Consider fixed IP (e.g., for corporate customers) as a permanent measure: cost will increase, but it is easier to avoid "misjudgment based on the history of reassigned IPs". ([NTT https://www.ntt.com/business/services/network/internet-connect/ocn-business/bocn/knowledge/archive_11.html?utm_source=chatgpt .com])
Summary (Analysis)

NURO itself distributes domestically registered IPs, and the misidentification is triggered by content side NURO itself distributes domestically registered IPs and the misidentification is triggered by the old DB. ([NURO Hikari https://www.nuro.jp/article/kaigai-ip/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

The country name SG is likely to appear because (a) SG is often used as the core PoP for APAC, (b) Anycast termination for Private Relay and public DNS is located in SG, and (c) IP blocks that were once operated in SG have been reassigned to the country, either/combined. ([The Cloudflare Blog https://blog.cloudflare.com/ja-jp/connection-errors-in-asia-pacific-region-on-july-9-2023/?utm_source=chatgpt. com])
If necessary, create a procedure (set of commands to copy and paste)** for **the quickest isolation in your current environment**.

uncommon ground
[GPT5.icon]
What does [Audrey Tang] mean by "uncommon ground" (based on actual statements)?
in a word

Tang repeatedly talks about this as a key concept for implementing plurality. Tang repeatedly talks about this as a key concept for implementation. ([rightlivelihood.org https://rightlivelihood.org/the-change-makers/find-a-laureate/audrey-tang/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Statement by Tang himself (short excerpt)

Technology allows us to find our "uncommon ground" (points of agreement that are rarely shared). This is said in the context of "being able to create policies and norms together from there." ([rightlivelihood.org https://rightlivelihood.org/the-change-makers/find-a-laureate/audrey-tang/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
The "uncommon ground" (of the public hearing and AI) will be uncovered and connected from people's different ideas. ([SayIt https://sayit.archive.tw/speech/622917?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

"Bridging Bonus algorithm increases visibility of "bridging statements" and extends bridges of agreement without inciting division by designing no reply button." ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
"[Polis] is a tool for finding uncommon ground." ([LessWrong https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/anoK4akwe8PKjtzkL/plurality-and-6pack-care?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

He also mentioned a specific example of a misinformation countermeasure: "We found UNCOMMON ground, so we were able to quickly pre-bank messages. ([yaschamounk.substack.com https://yaschamounk.substack.com/p/audrey-tang-on-misinformation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

By designing the right "place" and making **uncommon points of agreement** visible, the energy of conflict can be transformed into the energy of co-creation" ([MediaConnect ]). ([MediaConnect https://mediaconnect.com/audrey-tang-tokyos-role-in-a-world-of-rapid-change?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
How it works (summary)

1. broad listening: Collect opinions from a large group of people through Polis and other means. Avoid designing "punching each other" with replies and quotes, and focus on voting for and against and summarizing. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

2. bridging emphasis: a design that rewards bridging, i.e., floating bridging statements that attract support from both different opinion groups to the top of the list. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

(3) Consensus foundation → Practice: Based on the visualized "uncommon ground", connect to stakeholder meetings and regulatory design. ([Northwest Asian Weekly https://nwasianweekly.com/2025/02/taiwans-audrey-tang-shares-views-on-healthy-open-source-pro-social-ai/?utm _source=chatgpt.com])
representative example
Uber Regulation (vTaiwan)

It was stated that the policy is to organize the issues in Polis of thousands of people and reflect the agreed items in the new rules (including responses to "coherent blended volition"). ([info.vtaiwan.tw https://info.vtaiwan.tw/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Countermeasures against misinformation (pre-banking)

The practice of finding [points of agreement that are acceptable to both sides] and getting the message out quickly to limit fragmentation. ([yaschamounk.substack.com https://yaschamounk.substack.com/p/audrey-tang-on-misinformation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Public Space Design

Tang explained that [designing for non-replies] and [bridging visualization] are ideas that also run through collective knowledge tools such as Community Notes. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Difference from "[common ground]"
common ground = common sense assumptions that everyone originally shares.

Tang speaks of finding this in the design of tools and places as a framework for transforming fragmentation into co-creation. ([MediaConnect https://mediaconnect.com/audrey-tang-tokyos-role-in-a-world-of-rapid-change?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Points that are often misunderstood

This is not **moderation (taking the middle ground)**. The key point is that it "amplifies by design" claims that really overlap among different tribes. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Nor is it "AI decides." It is collective knowledge support to help humans build consensus. ([rebootdemocracy.ai https://rebootdemocracy.ai/blog/audrey-tang-ai-democracy?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
To dig even deeper.
Numerous references to "uncommon ground" in Tang's speech transcripts (SayIt): 2025-08-05 speech, 2025-09-25 speech, etc. ([SayIt https://sayit.archive.tw/speech/622917?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

The core of the concept is also discussed in the introduction to **Plurality (co-authored)** and on the awards page. ([rightlivelihood.org https://rightlivelihood.org/the-change-makers/find-a-laureate/audrey-tang/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Record of on-site application (vTaiwan website, Polis official blog). ([info.vtaiwan.tw https://info.vtaiwan.tw/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If necessary, identify and summarize examples of actual bridging statements in Uber cases.

pages.title: Artificial Intelligence in Deliberation: The AI Penalty and the Emergence of a New Deliberative Divide

lines.text: Artificial Intelligence in Deliberation: The AI Penalty and the Emergence of a New Deliberative Divide
https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07690
[Deliberative Divide]
[AI Penalty]
[GPT5.icon]

This study shows that there is an "AI penalty," i.e., a reduction in willingness to participate and "quality" ratings when AI is put forward. If designed and communicated incorrectly, it will create a new "AI attitude" that will lead to a new point of division.
Conclusions to be held
AI Penalty: When an AI is involved, the willingness to participate and quality rating is lowered on average (about -0.30/-0.29 on a 7-point scale).

Resistance is particularly high for "visible intervention" in summarizing, structuring issues, and collecting opinions. On the other hand, fact-checking is accepted to the same degree as human intervention.

Axis of division changes: participation is divided not by education or income, but by attitudes toward AI (those who believe in the social benefits of AI and anthropomorphize AI are less resistant / those who see strong AI risks are more resistant).
Who's Coming: Willingness to participate increases with political interest and Need for Cognition. The impact of resource factors such as time and education is smaller.
Assumptions: representative sample from Germany (2025/2). Can vary by culture and time period.
This AI penalty is going to be heavily influenced by culture and age.[nishio.icon]
Implementation guide (in order of no failures)
1. ai from "behind the scenes
First, translation assistance/vandalism detection/tone assistance/(with human verification) fact checking.
Summaries, issue maps, and opinion aggregation are introduced in stages & always clearly identified with human final confirmation.
2. selectable AI (Opt-in/Opt-out)
AI support toggle in participant UI, "AI Draft -> Human Confirmed" badge, and human facilitation limited room anytime.
3. transparency > performance
Intervention logs, evidence links, and version history are available. Microcopy of "AI is draft only/final decision is human" always displayed.
4. segment-specific security design
Guarantee an "AI-free" experience for AI skeptics. Guidance text should focus on fairness and visualization of voices rather than "efficiency.
5. expansion with measurement
A/B (AI vs. person) for each intervention, tracking (1) participation rate, (2) attrition rate, (3) statement diversity, and (4) 5-item trust and fairness index.
6. governance and resilience
SLAs for bias audits, data minimization, human override, and corrective procedures for failure are agreed upon in advance.
Checklist before, during and after the event
Previous: Table and publish which tasks will be handled by AI/humans/opt-out leads/small pilot.

Medium: Dashboard to monitor deviations / "people stop" button / 1-question pulse ("Is it fair to proceed now?") Middle: Dashboard monitoring of deviations / "people stop" button / one question pulse ("Is it fair to proceed now?")
After: evaluation by index of trust and fairness → stratified analysis by AI attitude x political interest → feedback on improvements to the next session.
Examples of ready-to-use display text (short sentences)
AI only produces a draft summary. A person will review it before it is published."
Use or not use AI assistance (can be toggled at any time)
**"**Final decisions are made by human consensus. **AI suggestions are for informational purposes only."
First Next Action (lightweight)
1. introduce only fact checking for translation support + human verification at the next event (summary and aggregation will not be included).
Add Opt-out to the above two functions and add a description and "confirmed" badge to the UI.
3. collect participation rate, withdrawal, and simple confidence score → check the difference between skeptical and non-skeptical groups to determine the next scope of expansion.

lines.text: Urgency as a pretext for authoritarianism
[urgency] as a pretext for [authoritarianism].
[GPT5.icon]
The following are key points extracted and organized from Audrey Tang (2021-04-06, interview with Arwa Mahdawi), focusing on "urgency / common (or shared) urgency" and "authoritarianism".
Summary (Conclusion)

Shared/common urgency (shared/common urgency) drives behavioral change: the pandemic experience showed that "resolution proceeds at record speed (vaccines, habit change) when humanity treats it as a shared urgency. He noted that this mode should be transferred to the climate crisis. ([SayIt])

Lack of common urgency is an obstacle in large areas: in areas where the disaster is not felt, it appears to be a "next generation issue" and movement is slow because it is not a common urgency. ([SayIt])

Authoritarianism damages "shared urgency": Authoritarianism hinders access to facts (e.g., Dr. Wenliang Li's warning went unheeded) and leads to the idea of "sacrificing some of our freedoms" in favor of authoritarianism in crisis response. Every time a society becomes authoritarian, innovation and facts are **diminished ("literally cut by 10 percent "**) and the formation of shared urgency is undercut. ([SayIt https://sayit.pdis.nat.gov.tw/speech/464113?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Alternatives: quick adoption cycle + safe collaborative space ("pro-social media/g0v/Join") to circuit pluralistic leadership that allows many parallel solutions is key (24-48h, citizen initiated -> nationwide (case study of deployment). ([SayIt])

Prerequisite Infrastructure: Broadband can only be "e-" and everyday participation is possible when public infrastructure such as human rights, digital competency, NHI apps, etc. are widespread. ([SayIt])
How the term is used (in this interview)
Urgency: A generic term for the psychological and social drive to feel that an issue should be handled "now.

common/shared urgency: A state of affairs in which the entire society simultaneously perceives the situation as "personal" and synchronizes its actions. Pandemics are a good example of this, and it is argued that this state of affairs should be created in the climate as well. ([SayIt])

（Although manufactured urgency is not discussed in this interview, Tang speaks of a design that fosters urgency as co-creation rather than "fabrication" through outside game (outside game) and rapid adoption. ([SayIt])
Relationship with Authoritarianism (Danger and Counter-axis)
Criticism of the trend toward "planned economy authoritarianism as the only solution" in response to pandemics, disinformation, and even climate change. ([SayIt])

Inhibit access to facts → urgency of sharing collapses: without freedom of the press, initial warnings do not reach society and the perception of sharing does not rise up (example of Li Wenliang). ([SayIt])

Authoritarian leadership leads to competition for a single solution, which reduces the speed and diversity of social implementation. Taiwan, on the other hand, has expanded (pralism) by design to allow parallel implementation. ([SayIt])
Design principles for creating "shared urgency" (excerpt)
1. safe collaborative space (fork the government) + rapid adoption (24-48h): citizen proposal -> government API -> nationwide deployment (mask map). ([SayIt])
2. moving the government "together with the people" in an outside game (not co-opt, but expand the voice). ([SayIt])
3. high bit rate of daily participation: voting once every 4 years = only "3 bits per person", making continuous participation and feedback within 60 days normalized by Join, etc. ([SayIt])

4. universalization of infrastructure: Broadband is a human right, "e-" will be removed when public digital infrastructure such as NHI apps are "over half the population" (digital democracy becomes routine). ([SayIt])
5. education is more competency than literacy: citizens acquire tolerance ("immunity") to disinformation by doing journalism and citizen science as a practice. ([SayIt])
Implementation image (suggested)
Crisis communication is not **"one company's right answer" but rather a decentralized extension (adoption not elimination) with APIs and parallel implementations**. ([SayIt])
Measure and improve bandwidth of participation (numerical operation of policy response cycle and visibility). ([SayIt])

Countermeasures against disinformation that does not "fall" into authoritarianism: Foster an urgency for sharing through factual access, transparency, and co-translation/co-authorship ("pro-social media"), rather than bulk deletion from above ([SayIt]). ([SayIt])

lines.text: Generative AI and Public Deliberation: A Framework for LLM-augmented Digital Democracy
https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3737/paper33.pdf
[GPT5.icon]
What is [neurosymbolic reasoning]?

This method integrates neural (deep learning) pattern recognition with symbolic (logic, rules, knowledge graphs) symbolic reasoning, aiming to combine the generative power of LLM with the consistency and verifiability of KG and logic to increase factuality and explainability. The definition in the paper also clearly states that it is "a hybrid of symbolic reasoning while utilizing the power of neural.
General commentary and surveys also show the position that neural x symbolic integration improves robustness and interpretability
[Neuro-symbolic approaches in artificial intelligence - PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35673530/]
[GPT5.icon]
Short Summary:

Purpose: Existing digital deliberations are limited in quality and scale due to information overload, lack of knowledge, and hesitancy to speak up. The authors propose a framework to enhance participation, trust, and evidence-based decision making using LLM. eGOV-CeDEM-ePart 2024 accepted.

Proposal: "LLM-KG framework" integrating LLM + [knowledge graph] (KG) + [neuro-symbolic reasoning]. It combines generativity (LLM) and logical consistency/factuality (KG/symbolic reasoning) to ensure explainability.

Bridging: combination of CoT, RAG, few-shot, prompt design, fine-tuning, and neuro-symbolic reasoning, with data preprocessing, transformation, monitoring, and indexing in the lower layers. A conceptual diagram (Figure 1) is presented.

Function set (assistant service): (1) fact checking, (2) information retrieval, (3) argument construction (assembling arguments and evidence), (4) summarization, (5) contradiction detection, (6) role playing, (7) explanation generation and reporting, (8) collective decision support.

Implications of related research: LLM is promising for argument summarization/argument generation, etc., but issues remain such as halcination, sensitivity to input/output expressions and prompts, lack of interpretability, and impact of toxicity data. xAI and KG integration has not been fully explored.
Example 1 (Fact checking): Extracting claims from input text → triples (triples) → KG inquiry → mock-up presenting supporting facts (Figure 2).
Example 2 (Argument construction): Extract assumptions from citizens' input → Triplicate → Obtain relevant evidence from KG and construct a mock-up of claims and evidence (Figure 3).

Conclusion: Based on human-machine collaboration, this study demonstrates the social impact of deliberation and its potential for restoring trust. Future needs planned implementation according to the resources of public organizations and rigorous evaluation with appropriate KPIs.
(Keywords: LLM, digital democracy, deliberation, knowledge graph, neuro-symbolic AI)
[nishio.icon]Is this just a suggestion? Have you experimented?
[GPT5.icon]

Evaluation: preliminary assessment / up to the first stage of practitioner validation (positive). Full-scale operational experimentation and quantitative KPI evaluation are clearly identified as future work.
Conclusion: This paper is up to framework proposal + stakeholder evaluation + mock-up demonstration, full-scale implementation and quantitative experiments have not been reported.

PVC Algorithm
from  [Nodal Point of Thought 2025-10-10]
PVC Algorithm
[Proportional Veto Core
Something (Definition)
Voters (n) persons and candidates (m) names. The coalition (T) (number of people (|T|=k)) is given the right to veto,
[$ v(T)=\left\lfloor \frac{m\cdot |T|}{n} \right\rfloor-1]
A candidate can be dropped from the race (proportional rejection principle). ([AAAI https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/16691/16691-13-20185-1-2-20210518.pdf])
A coalition is an arbitrary subset of voters[nishio.icon]

For candidate (c), a coalition (T) can block (c) if it has a large enough "candidate set (B) that all members consider above (c). A candidate who is not blocked by any coalition is a PVC (proportional rejection core).
[nishio.icon]
The condition is [$ |B| \ge m - v(T)].
Voters (n=100) persons and candidates (m=10) persons. If coalition (T) (number of people (|T|=k=30)) then v(T) = floor(10 * 30/100) - 1 which is 2
If 30 people agree that "Candidate C is no good" (there are at least 8 better candidates than C), the remaining 70 people can reject Candidate C, even if they had voted for it, which is how it works.
Key Nuances
No affirmative agreement required: the coalition does not have to agree on "this one", only that there are enough "better" candidates than c to drop c.
Counterfactual criterion: It is not necessary for a coalition to actually be formed, but rather, "if such a coalition can exist, then c is inadequate. This is the "core" concept.
Example of intuition: when m=n+1, a coalition with number k can reject exactly k candidates

Origin: classical results by Moulin (1981) presenting the "proportional rejection principle" and showing that the core is not always empty (at least one candidate remains). ([JSTOR https://www.jstor.org/stable/2297154?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Intuition: x% of the coalition can drop about x% of the candidates, so this is a mechanism to avoid a situation where a minority is forced to choose the worst candidate based solely on simple majority rule.
A naive implementation will result in an "arbitrary subset", so[$ 2^n]のオーダーになって無理なんだが、多項式時間で解ける[nishio.icon]
What is the "PVC Algorithm" (the gist of the calculation method)
Ianovski & Kondratev (AAAI-21) presented an algorithm to compute PVC in polynomial time:
For each candidate (c), "Is there a ((T,B)) that can block (c)?" is determined by attributing it to maximum flow / maximum complete bipartite graph detection.
Run for all candidates to obtain the unblockable candidate set = PVC.
The computational complexity is ([$ O!\left(m\cdot\max(n^3,m^3)\right)]). ([AAAI https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/16691/16691-13-20185-1-2-20210518.pdf])

An anonymous/neutral core selection procedure called Veto by Consumption (in which each voter continuously whittles away the "take points" of his or her lowest-ranking candidate to select the last remaining candidate) has also been proposed. ([AAAI https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/16691/16691-13-20185-1-2-20210518.pdf])
Where is it used?
Design and Analysis of Single-Winner Elections with an Emphasis on Minority Protection. ([AAAI https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/16691/16691-13-20185-1-2-20210518.pdf])

Applications: An algorithm (Rank-Core-Fed) has also been proposed to extend PVC as a fairness concept for **Federated Learning** and to learn PVC-stable models. ([Proceedings of Machine Learning Research https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/ray-chaudhury24a.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Stratified random sampling
[GPT5.icon]

In short, it is a method of "[stratification]" ([stratification]) and random sampling and allocation within each stratum. Formal terms include "stratified random sampling" or "[stratified randomization]" depending on the context.
What do you do?
1. stratified random sampling (statistical survey)
The population was divided into strata by age, region, gender, etc., and randomly selected within each stratum.
→ Reduce the variance of the estimation while ensuring the inclusion of a small segment of the population.
(Weighted estimation: composite averages by proportion of each layer)
2. stratified randomization (clinical trial)
Stratified by prognostic factors (age group, institution, etc.) and randomized to treatment group by stratum.
→ Improved group balance. Often combined with block randomization.
3. stratified sampling (Monte Carlo)
The area of integration is divided into subcompartments (strata) and a random sample from each stratum.
→ Dispersion reduction method to reduce variation (dispersion).
4. stratified cross-validation (machine learning)
Split to keep the class ratio at each fold (Stratified K-Fold).
→ Stabilized evaluation with unbalanced data.
When to use it?
Want to ensure inclusion of an important but small number of subgroups
I want to reduce the precision (variance) of the estimation
I would like to make an evaluation that maintains class imbalance.
Want to reduce background differences between intervention groups (test)
important point
Excessive subdivision of layers leads to under-sampling of each layer
Weighting is necessary if extraction probabilities differ by layer
It is customary to adjust the layers in the test for covariates in the analytical model as well.

lines.text: History of subdivisions of the public goods concept
[https://gyazo.com/cdf839011e493fe071e281ba4135fa78]
[nishio.icon]
There is a commonplace naive concept A
A companion to A, but realizing that there is something out of the ordinary A, we can create concept B.
A and B in the narrow sense are antithetical to each other
Related concept C appears.
A and C conflict on attribute X, B and C conflict on attribute Y
There is a 2x2 matrix and the empty space is named concept D
A simpler version
[The two boundaries are not parallel.]
[GPT5.icon]
It is a nice abstraction. The following dynamics, when viewed as a "type" of development, are running.
Deciphering the Pattern
1.[naive concept]A (prototype stage)
A large box that "looks like" a large number of phenomena. Boundaries are vague and judgments are based on similarity.
2. surfacing of [Exception] → cutting out B (institutionalization of anomalous cases)
A lump of "not ordinary A" repeatedly appears in A, and the essential condition of A is verbalized.
→ Narrow A and B become exclusionary (evidence of clarification of boundaries).
3. introduction of orthogonal properties → appearance of C (discovery of dimension)
It is not enough to explain A and B. A new attribute (X, Y) is found.
In an attempt to describe the difference between A and B, we see that there are two alternatives[nishio.icon]
A and C are in conflict at X, B and C are in conflict at Y, and so on, the biaxial structure stands.
At this stage, the classification qualitatively shifted from "naming" to "coordinating.
4. naming a 2 × 2 negative space → D (theoretically complete)
A blank quadrant is created in the coordinate plane. The symmetry of the theory suggests that "there must be a type there too.
Re-naming if examples already exist, otherwise defining D as a future discovery/design target.
Conditions under which this mold works well
Axis validity: X and Y should be substantial, measurable, and as independent (orthogonal) as possible.
Operational definition: X and Y determination procedures can be shared (can be qualitative, but must be reproducible).
Predictive Power: By including D, the unobserved nature and implications of the institutional design can be predicted anew.
Robustness: explanatory power does not decrease when the domain changes (even in a different domain).

Tolerance to temporal change: X/Y will move with technology and institutions (e.g., DRM will artificially increase "excludability" / congestion will make "competitiveness" a continuous value). Extensibility to handle continuations and hybrids is necessary.
Risks and Cautions

Filling in the blanks" is the first step in the creation of a nominal category: D will be hollowed out if it is hastily created only for the "convenience of symmetry". Support with examples, measurements, and forecasts.
2 x 2 overconfidence: really more than 3 axes are needed, or the axes may be context-dependent.
Boundary roughness: do not force continuous and condition-dependent (e.g., "crowded and competitive") to be binary.
To apply this to the example of public goods (a suggested correspondence)
A = naive image of public good (non-competitive)
B = Club goods (cut out "public-looking but different")
C = Common Pool Resources (Appearance of a strong sense of competitiveness)
Axis = X: Competitiveness (depletion) / Y: Excludability
D = private good (explicitly positioned as the remaining quadrant in the theoretical coordinates)
The historical order is not necessarily A→B→C→D, but the idea is to coordinate the conceptual space and make it complete, including the "blanks".
[nishio.icon]
No, first of all, there's A: goods.
B: Samuelson (1954) formulated pure public goods by defining "joint consumption (noncompetitiveness)",
At this time, only attribute X (competitiveness) was verbalized
But attribute Y is verbalized.
Y: Musgrave (1959) presents "(non)exclusiveness"
Thereby C: Buchanan (1965) presents "club goods (excludable x non-competitive)
Finally D: Ostrom Common Pool Resources (non-exclusion x conflict)
[GPT5.icon]
Yes, that sequence is nearly accurate. Supplemental only:
B (1954): Samuelson formulated pure public goods with "joint consumption = noncompetitiveness". Axis of competitiveness (non-competitiveness) clarified first.

Y (1959): Musgrave articulated the "principle of exclusion" (includability) in his theory of public property. Later, the two criteria of "non-competition × non-exclusion" were also crystallized in Musgrave's system.
C (1965): Buchanan presents club goods (excludable x noncompetitive). Crowding (partial competition) also analyzed.

D (1977/1990): Ostrom & Ostrom present 2 x 2 exclusionary x depletable (competitive) and clearly position **Common pool resources (non-exclusionary x competitive)** Ostrom (1990) systematizes institutional design.

However, the D entity (common resource) itself was already raised in Gordon's (1954) "Common Fishery" and Hardin's (1968) "The Tragedy of Common Land" before Ostrom. Ostrom established it theoretically as CPR and incorporated it into 2×2. ([economia.unam.mx https://www.economia.unam.mx/profesores/blopez/bienestar-ScottGordonFisheries.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
In a nutshell: the axis (non-competition → elimination) was verbalized first, then club goods were introduced, and finally the CPR was established as a "blank quadrant" in a 2 x 2 framework.

pages.title: A functioning institution itself is a public good.

lines.text: A functioning institution itself is a public good.
What is the "functioning institutions themselves are public goods" kind of talk in the context of OSTROM?[nishio.icon]
[GPT5.icon]

In short, the "functioning institutions (public goods)" in the Ostrom system are those in which, once the "set of rules operating mechanisms" (boundary setting, monitoring, sanctions, dispute resolution, recording and visualization, a place to renew agreements, etc.) that make resource management possible are in place, all parties involved benefit at the same time, and thus behave in a non-competitive and non-excluding manner internally. Once in place, all parties benefit at the same time, so they behave in a non-competitive and non-exclusionary manner internally.
Ostrom often treats this as a "[second-order collective action problem].
Why "public goods"?

It is the rules-in-use and the institutional apparatus of monitoring, sanctioning, dispute resolution, etc. that support the rules-in-use that order the collection and use of individual users (the primary issue).
When it works, if someone pays for the maintenance and upkeep, other members can receive the same quality of order benefits (free ride is likely to occur) -> public goods-like.
*The key point is that in a community with clear member boundaries, it works internally as a public good, although externally it is excludable and thus has an aspect similar to a "club good".
Prescription for secondary problems (free ride on institutional supply)
Ostrom's field studies suggest that the following design will enhance the sustainability of the system itself (corresponding to the "eight principles")
1. clear boundaries and alignment of resources and burdens
Consensus building with user participation (collective-choice)
3. mutual monitoring (the observer is responsible to the parties)
4. graduated sanctions
5. low-cost dispute resolution forum
6. recognition of autonomy by an external authority
7. nested enterprises
8. making **common knowledge** through recording and visualization
concrete example
Waterway associations: water distribution rules, patrols, progressive sanctions for violations, duty system
Fisheries cooperatives: agreement on no-take zones and fishing seasons, mutual monitoring, dispute arbitration
Knowledge Commons/OSS: Submission norms, maintenance system, review authority, publication of history and proceedings
Practical implications (incentive design)
Institutions tend to dilute the private returns of their suppliers because they are public goods. Therefore,
Role visibility and credit/reputation (honorary positions, maintenance authority)
Fair allocation of expenses (dues, labor, tokens, etc.)
Reduced monitoring costs (logs, sensors, public dashboards)
Regular agreement renewal cycle
and other measures to reduce "[secondary free rides]" and develop the system itself into a sustainable public good.

Lent loss
[GPT5.icon]
[Lent] dissipation" in the Ostrom context.
Definition.

The excess benefits (resource rents) that would normally be obtained if the system were in place (CPR: fisheries, forests, irrigation water, etc.) in common resources (CPR: fisheries, forests, irrigation water, etc.),
A phenomenon that burns out to near zero due to unrestricted entry, over-extraction, competition for location, competition for equipment, conflict costs, etc.
Why it happens (structure of CPR)
Difficult to exclude → does not stop entry (OPEN ACCESS).
Competitive consumption (subtractability) → Preemptive competition occurs because the extraction of others reduces one's gain.
As a result, costs that do not increase efficiency (equipment augmentation, night watch, surveillance avoidance, and conflict) increase and rents disappear.
Contrast with public goods (Ostrom's two types)
Public goods: underprovision (free ride).
Shared resources: overutilization (rent loss).
→ Both require institutional design, but the direction of distortion is opposite.
Mini formulas (for intuition)
Resource Rent ≈ Total Revenue - Total Cost - Normal Profit.
Optimal Management (MEY): Rent > 0.
Unregulated entry: profit π → 0 (average income = average cost) due to competition → rent loss.
typical pattern
The "equipment/speed race" in the fishing industry: catch does not increase much, but only costs increase.
Irrigation "upstream preemption + downstream duty/increased pumping": no growth in total gain, but increased labor and conflict costs.
Ostrom's solution (Rent preservation system)
Design principles are addressed:
1. clear boundaries (delineation of members and resource areas)
2. resource and rule compliance (limitation of amount collected, season, tools)
3. rule formation for party participation
4. surveillance (mutual monitoring by peers)
5. graduated sanctions
6. dispute resolution forum
7. approval by external authorities (authorization for self-management)
8. multi-tiered governance (wide area is coordinated at higher levels)
→ Transform open access into a shared "property" regime to reduce over-competition and keep rents within the community.
Differences from related concepts
[rent-seeking] (Tullock): wasteful spending resulting from the competition for political privileges.
Lent loss (CPR): wastage caused by competition for access to and extraction of natural resources. Different starting points, but common in wasting social surpluses.
In a nutshell, Ostrom's institutional design prevents "[umami burnout].

lines.text: When you want LLM to process Japanese

[nishio.icon]Is there any research on which is better in situations where we want LLMs to read Japanese and output in Japanese, the English prompt "output in Japanese" or the Japanese translation of the prompt? I'm thinking about applications where non-English speakers are the primary users, not necessarily Japanese speakers.
[GPT5.icon]
https://chatgpt.com/c/68ec8fde-f364-8321-a7e9-437d93c9b69d

Abstract: Recent research has concluded that there is no uniform optimal solution to the question of whether to instruct "output in Japanese" in English or to write in Japanese from the beginning, and that the choice depends on the nature of the task and the data. The following is a practical criterion.
What we see from the study (super summary)
A fair comparison shows that English is not the sole winner. Compared by design without translationese,
English instructions are slightly more favorable for reading comprehension systems (MRC),
Target language (Japanese) instructions are advantageous for lexical simplification, etc,
Classification is advantageous to align the language of labels with the language of instructions,
The report also shows that English instructions are more stable in terms of compliance with complex instructions.

Selective pre-translation," in which only a portion of the prompt is translated into English (instructions, examples, context, etc.), is on average the strongest (35 languages x multiple tasks, large scale test).

It is possible that they are "thinking" in English internally. Based on the analysis of multi-layered representations, we propose the hypothesis (MWork) that in the middle layer, the inference is centered on English, and in the final layer, the inference is returned to the original language. This is the basis for the design to utilize the English component in difficult inferences.

There are tasks where the method of using English only for reasoning is effective. The EN-CoT/XLT system of "Japanese question → step-by-step thinking in English → final answer in Japanese" reported improvements in arithmetic, common sense reasoning, NLI, etc.

Some experiments show that in certain domains (e.g., Arabic SNS classification), non-native language (English) instructions are superior on average. Although generalizations are prohibited, there are certainly cases of "English instruction dominance.

10/19/2012 Before and after

Open Hack Day 2012] hastily created and won an award for a visualization of the central government's total budget (Budget Maps); CL Kao registered g0.v.tw as a domain "for remixing government sites by citizens. v.tw as a "domain for remixing government sites by citizens. This is the beginning of what is commonly referred to as "unauthorized forking. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G0v_movement])

The "Zeroth (Hackath0n)" was held. Since then, the bimonthly large-scale hackathons have taken root, and a culture has spread that "if you replace .gov with .g0v, you can go to the shadow government site". ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G0v_movement])

**Permanent projects, such as the Legislative Council Portal (ly.g0v.tw), are launched, and the "parallel implementation -> improvement proposals (fork -> merge)** kineticism is solidified, including cross-search and comparison of bills and proceedings, and visualization of voting results. Since 2014 (Sunflower Movement)

Key Points (Organizing the Historical Process)

Method: Instead of "hacking" to alter the official site, citizens build their own "shadow version" on a separate domain based on public information (avoiding legal risks and ensuring criticality). The watchword is fork → merge back (if you like) ([g0v.github.io https://g0v.github.io/g0v.us/tw/])

pages.title: Don't ask what your country can do for you. Ask what you can do for your country.

lines.text: Don't ask what your country can do for you. Ask what you can do for your country.
[GPT5.icon]

To summarize briefly - this is a line from [J.F. Kennedy's] inaugural address on January 20, 1961, in which he called for a civic duty to shift our consciousness "from thinking of ourselves as beneficiaries to contributing as citizens. The message is a call to civic duty. The original text is

"Ask not what your country can do for you-ask what you can do for your country." (followed by "My fellow citizens of the world ..." (followed by "My fellow citizens of the world ..." and a sentence that extends to citizens of the world). ([National Archives https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/president-john-f-kennedys-inaugural-address?utm_source=chatgpt.com ])
What's Good (Rhetoric)

Antimetabole, the use of tautology with word order inversion, and anastrophe ("Ask not ...") make for a memorable couplet. ([LitCharts https://www.litcharts.com/literary-devices-and-terms/antimetabole?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Background and Intent

In the context of the generational shift in the early years of the [Cold War] "the torch has been passed to a new generation," emphasis was placed on public service, volunteerism, tax payment, military service, and other public service. In fact, the **Peace Corps** was created by Executive Order that year. ([JFK Library https://www.jfklibrary.org/archives/other-resources/john-f-kennedy-speeches/inaugural-address-19610120?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
Related: [A New Cold War].
Common misconceptions and nuances in Japanese translation

"country" refers to a country = community broader than the government (government). It is natural to read it as a motto urging "compatibility of rights and responsibilities," rather than a statement denying the demand for rights. At the end of the speech, he also expands the phrase to cooperation beyond national interests, saying, "It is not what the United States can do for you, but what we can do together for freedom. ([National Archives https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/president-john-f-kennedys-inaugural-address?utm_source=chatgpt.com ])
Prior representation (not just "JFK originals")

O.W. Holmes, Jr. (1884 Memorial Day speech) has a close syntax, "[Recall] what our country has done for us, and ask ourselves what we can give back to it." ([Internet Archive https://archive.org/download/cu31924014419547/cu31924014419547.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[W.G. Harding] (1916) also said, "[What the government can do for the country rather than what it does for us]." ([wist.info https://wist.info/harding-warren/50932/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
>In the great fulfillment we must have a citizenship less concerned about what the government can do for it and more anxious about what it can do for the nation.
This is using government and nation interchangeably.[nishio.icon]

There is also a passage in [Khalil Jibran] (1925, "[New Borders]"), "Are you a politician who asks what your country does to you, or a politician who asks what you do to your country?", which is often linked to JFK's motto (although the borrowing is never confirmed). ([The Poetry Foundation https://www.poetryfoundation.org/articles/88761/governing-rhetoric?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
How to take it (practical reading)

This is not a slogan to silence individual demands, but a call to be aware of our role as actors in creating public goods together. In particular, it indicates a preference for actions that **"add" rather than "receive "**, such as voting, community activism, participation in public services, and collaboration on global issues (freedom and human rights). The overall tone of the speech is also in this direction. ([JFK Library https://www.jfklibrary.org/archives/other-resources/john-f-kennedy-speeches/inaugural-address-19610120?utm_source= chatgpt.com])

In short, this sentence is a masterpiece of civic ethics, beautifully crafted in both syntax and meaning, that in one stroke prompts a shift in perspective from "recipient dependent on the state" to "co-producer of the public".

The design is also detailed using AI, and the work process is collected in a master document, which is updated each time the work is done, so that the progress of development can be viewed in a series.

> Furthermore, even at the stage of actually implementing the created code, the AI agent checks that there are no problems and verifies that there are no bugs by actually running the code while formulating various hypotheses and examining them. Even the best programmers cannot achieve this kind of productivity, and this work throughput will continue to increase exponentially.

[nishio.icon]Instead of having Polis-like data on each individual's vote and calculating the correlation, summarize it as data on the percentage of agreement or disagreement for each individual question and use it as a one-dimensional measure of more or less agreement?
[gpt5.icon]Yes, that understanding is almost OK.

Sensemaker does not create correlations or clusters (Polis Opinion Groups type) based on individual x statement voting vectors, but only on the aggregate ratio of agree/disagree/pass for each statement to select statements suitable for "Common Ground/Differences of Opinion". The small sample is used to avoid misinterpretation. Small samples are excluded if the total number of votes is less than 20 to avoid misinterpretation. The text is used only for "topic selection and assignment" and not for the agreement/difference selection itself.

In addition, Relative Agreement is calculated by comparing "the number of statements in the Common Ground/the total number of statements in that subtopic" in each subtopic relative to other subtopics and assigning a High/Low value to each subtopic. --In other words, here again, it is treated as a one-dimensional "strength of agreement" indicator.

Step 2 - Apply grouping criteria:.
Combine claims into the same group if they share any of the following: 1.

✓ Identical recommendations/solutions (even if differently reasoned)
✓ Same values and principles expressed
✓ Different aspects of the same topic (e.g., "high cost" + "unclear price" = price concerns)

summary

Definition (closer to practice): the state/ability of a democratic society to continuously avoid factors that threaten the process of producing, distributing, acquiring, and evaluating reliable knowledge. The Turning Institute report formulates this as a challenge to the "resilience of the social epistemic infrastructures" of society. ([turing.ac.uk https://www.turing.ac.uk/news/publications/tackling-threats-informed-decision-making-democratic-societies?utm_source =chatgpt.com])

Positioning in policy context: The UK think tank Demos summarizes that at the national level it is "about ensuring the health of the information supply chains" (the report positions the term as having been coined by researchers at DSTL, Cambridge University, and the Turning Laboratory in 2020). (The report positions that this term was organized by the DSTL, University of Cambridge, and the Turning Institute in 2020). ([Demos https://demos.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Epistemic-Security-2029_accessible.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
What threatens the "knowledge security" of society (typical example)?

Systematic disinformation/manipulation of information, de-authorization of specialized knowledge, growing distrust of knowledge production and distribution institutions, extreme fragmentation, censorship, suppression of diverse perspectives, abuse of generative AI and persuasive AI, etc. ([Elizabeth Seger https://elizabethseger.com/epistemic-security/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Relationship to Audrey Tang (Tang Feng) (as confirmed by primary sources)

Tang referred to "human attention and epistemic security" as one of the pillars of AI research in the dialogue transcript ("human attention and epistemic security"). The term is used directly. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/8765?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

He also reiterated that the reduction of "epistemic injustice" ([epistemic injustice]) will be incorporated into the government's AI evaluation framework (AI evaluation centers to inspect AI for fictionalization and epistemic injustice). This is an example of implementation of institutional preservation of "knowledge security". ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/9411?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
As a practical operation, it was established in Taiwan.

"humor over rumor (2-2-2)": a 20-minute, 200-word, 2-image quick response operation to "happily" counteract the rumor. ([Guardian https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2021/feb/17/humour-over-rumour-taiwan-fake-news?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Cofacts: citizen-driven, open-source fact-checking infrastructure (messaging-driven verification community). ([Cornell Tech https://tech.cornell.edu/news/crowdsourced-fact-checking-fights-misinformation-in-taiwan/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

vTaiwan/Polis: Visualizing "rough consensus" for each issue and strengthening the foundation for consensus building (i.e., social cognitive infrastructure). ([blog.pol.is https://blog.pol.is/uber-responds-to-vtaiwans-coherent-blended-volition-3e9b75102b9b?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Cognitive Security: A defense concept (developed by NATO and others) that protects the realm of the mind against attacks and influence operations that target a person's cognition itself (attention, judgment, and behavior). Scale of practice:.
The starting point is an idea (ideation) at the town or school district level, where specific proper nouns, such as "a village of 100 people" scale, are used.

Definition (scale of policy and operation)

The concept focuses on the governance of "places" (neighborhoods, school districts, shopping districts, BIDs, etc.) that are subordinate to cities and prefectures, where the entities (residents, businesses, NPOs, local government departments, etc.) of the community concerned collaborate in decision-making and management. The standard reference point is "[Hyperlocal: Place Governance in a Fragmented World]" by [Brookings]. Public and media attention is biased toward acute and dramatic topics due to the "[problem attention] cycle" ([Downs]), and [chronic issues tend to be buried]. Thick Alignment
[GPT5.icon]
What is Thick Alignment ([Thick Alignment])?

A concept that "goes beyond single indicator optimization or benchmark conformity (=thin/thin) to [sociotechnical] alignment, including value context, power relations, institutions, operational procedures, and accountability. [Alondra Nelson] proposes a shift to a "thicker alignment" because the traditional "thin" alignment is too narrow in scope. ([oxford-aiethics.ox.ac.uk https://www.oxford-aiethics.ox.ac.uk/overview-ethics-ai-annual-lecture-alondra-nelson?utm_source=chatgpt .com])
Why is it necessary (Limitations of "thin")

Thin alignment = conformity to specified goals and evaluation axes is essential, but real values are multidimensional and situation-dependent, and dropping context and parties' meaning-making distorts them ([Goodhart-ization], [optimization without consensus], etc.). Recent discussions also emphasize both thin criteria + thick context. ([Brookings https://www.brookings.edu/articles/hype-and-harm-why-we-must-ask-harder-questions-about-ai-and-its-alignment-with-human -values/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Four components of thickness (shortest frame)
1.[Thick Description

An interpretive attitude that describes not only the act itself, but also the meaning and background given to the act by the parties involved ([Clifford Geertz]). It is a prerequisite for requirements definition and evaluation design. ([philpapers.org https://philpapers.org/archive/geettd.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2. "Contextual Integrity

The theory that privacy and fairness norms should follow domain-specific [context norms] ([Nissenbaum]). Align data design, information flow, and access privileges with place norms. ([nissenbaum.tech.cornell.edu https://nissenbaum.tech.cornell.edu/papers/H.%20Nissenbaum%2C%20_Privacy%20as%20Contextual%20 Integrity.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. "Co-alignment" with the system

A design that ties not only AI but also institutions, organizations, and procedures to the same value model ("[Thick Models of Value]"/[Full-Stack Alignment]"). Have representations and operations that allow both people and institutions to handle value. ([openreview.net https://openreview.net/pdf?id=SiE7WpC0eC&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
4. participation and accountability

Continued participation of stakeholders in design, operation, and audit, and external visibility of the basis for decision-making (procedures + depth of explanation); central to Nelson's problem statement. ([oxford-aiethics.ox.ac.uk https://www.oxford-aiethics.ox.ac.uk/overview-ethics-ai-annual-lecture-alondra-nelson?utm_source=chatgpt .com])
Checklist for implementation (for the field)

Value Card: "Values, Concerns, and Tolerances" for each party involved are written out thickly (THICK DESCRIPTION) and the areas of conflict are clearly indicated. ([philpapers.org https://philpapers.org/archive/geettd.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Contextual matrix: information flow conformance is inspected on 5 axes: data subject/sender/receiver/information type/transmission principle (contextual integrity). ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contextual_integrity?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Institutional hooks: API policy, recordkeeping obligations, objections, roles and authorities, and risk receptors are implemented institutionally (the "thick" foundation). ([openreview.net https://openreview.net/pdf?id=SiE7WpC0eC&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Two-tiered evaluation:
Thin = accuracy, effectiveness, SLA

Thick = Process/impact indicators such as distribution equity, accountability, vulnerable reach, and degree of consensus building. ([Brookings https://www.brookings.edu/articles/hype-and-harm-why-we-must-ask-harder-questions-about-ai-and-its-alignment-with-human -values/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Guiatu and thick description
[giats] and [thick description].
[GPT5.icon]
Geertz ([Clifford Geertz]) and "Thick Description ([Thick Description])"
Yes? (In a word)

This is a method of description that includes not only "what happened" but also what meaning is given to the action by the people involved. **[Culture = a web of meaning that people weave for themselves]** is the premise of this approach, which emphasizes "interpretation" rather than causal law. ([cdn.angkordatabase.asia https://cdn.angkordatabase.asia/libs/docs/clifford-geertz-the-interpretation-of-cultures.pdf?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
authority

The philosopher [Gilbert Ryle]'s term was developed as a methodology for anthropology by Giertz in his seminal paper "Thick Description: Toward an Interpretive Theory of Culture" (in "Hermeneutics of Culture", 1973). ([Moodle Scienze Umane https://ssu.elearning.unipd.it/pluginfile.php/942448/mod_folder/content/0/Pagine%20da%20Gilbert%20Ryle%20-%20 Collected%20Papers%2C%20Volume%202_%20Collected%20Essays%201929%20-%201968%20%282009%29.pdf?forcedownload=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com ])
Famous parable (wink vs. blink)

The same "eyelid twitch" can have a drastically different social meaning depending on whether it is an involuntary twitch or a wink to a peer. A basic example of how a "thin" description is only about movement, while a "thick" description deals with intention, norm, and context. ([Cultural Geography 340 https://culturalgeography340ua2014.files.wordpress.com/2014/01/thick-description-clifford-geertz.pdf?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])
How to write? (Practical tips)
(1) Gather concepts that are "[experience-near]" in the [vocabulary of the people involved].
(2) Check for discrepancies by going back and forth with the researcher's concept of "[experience-distant]" (i.e., the researcher's side).

(iii) Locate the event in the [symbolic system]. ([elearning.unito.it https://elearning.unito.it/scuolacle/pluginfile.php/218206/mod_resource/content/1/Geertz%20-%20dal%20punto%20 di%20vista%20dei%20nativi.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Typical application: Balinese cockfighting

In "Deep Play: Notes on the Balinese Cockfight," the betting, winning and losing are read as a play of masculinity, status, and fate, and cockfighting is "thickly" depicted as a social self-interpretation ([JSTOR ]). ([JSTOR https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/20024056.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
What is "thin"?

Enumerating observable behaviors and reducing them to a single indicator is "thin. Thick" descriptions deal with layers of meaning, power relations, and norms, and present the text as to why the interpretation is valid. ([cdn.angkordatabase.asia https://cdn.angkordatabase.asia/libs/docs/clifford-geertz-the-interpretation-of-cultures.pdf?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
Discussion and Limitations

Often criticized as leaning toward [relativism] (how to have universal standards), the discussion around Geertz also connects to ethics/relativism theory. The trick is to be aware of the presentation of evidence and disprovability in operation. ([Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/relativism/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
The shortest temps for immediate use
1. write down the meaning of the event in the language used by the people in the place (experiential proximity).
2. duplicate and buttress the researcher's framework (empirical remoteness).
3. support with evidence (utterances, objects, conventions) for whom and why it reads that way.
4. write alongside alternative interpretations and in which context the validity changes.
This is directly related to hyperlocal measures and "thick alignment". If necessary, we will create a thick description -> evaluation indicator template for your case on the spot.

Crowdsourced Adaptive Surveys
[PDF https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/EC492E9F650ADB1A24CBF49F93540436/S1047198724000342a.pdf/crowdsourced-adaptive-surveys.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com]
[Yamil Ricardo Velez]
in a word

CSAS (Crowdsourced Adaptive Surveys) = A "self-adaptive survey" that uses LLM to convert participants' open-ended comments into questions, and then optimizes the "questions to be asked" in real-time using Multi-Arm Bandit. This makes it difficult to miss new issues and community-specific interests.
What's new?
Difference from CAT: CAT is for "precision measurement of existing scales"; CSAS allows the question pool itself to grow from participant input, capturing unknown discrete issues.
Difference from Wiki survey: Wiki is mainly paired comparisons; CSAS automatically adjusts search ⇔ utilization with Bandit for continuous/sequential scale grading (e.g., importance and accuracy).
Mechanism (pipeline)
1. collect free descriptions
2. questioning in LLM (e.g., one-sentence summary)
Filter: Neighborhood search by embedding → Duplicate removal (threshold 0.90)/Toxicity removal
4. participants graded: own questions + k from existing

5. selection optimization: Gaussian Thompson Sampling (GTS) to increase the probability of presenting questions with high average scores (but with a probability floor of 0.01, leaving new and few questions)
The idea of being adaptive about which questions you pose is[Polis question presentation order mechanism] とも関連している[nishio.icon]
6. estimation: IPW corrected by the inverse of the presentation probability to estimate the mean, etc.
What we saw from the demonstration (abstract)
Issue Salience（N=820, 2023/9/11–13）

Economic and medical items directly related to daily life, such as cost of living, medical care, and economy, are at the top of the list; participant-generated items (e.g., privacy protection, candidate transparency, mental health) are often higher than the fixed categories in the Gallup.
Misinfo for Latino (N=319, 7/6/2023-7)

Actual events and partisan stereotypes are rated more "accurate," while outright falsehoods are rated lower. Moreover, participant-generated claims are more likely to uncover "believable" items** than existing fact-checking sources.
local politics
While local and national issues can be mixed in, concerns specific to the region can also be automatically uncovered.
forte
Adaptation speed: Immediate incorporation into the pool when new topics are introduced.
Inductive design: can pick up on the researcher's assumptions
Participatory: subjects co-create surveys
Cost efficiency: search a large number of questions even in a small number of slots (inference cost estimate is about $0.005-$0.01 per person)
Points to keep in mind, limitations and countermeasures
"Late arrival" questions are disadvantageous: probability floor, initial search quota, batch introduction
Adjustment of similarity threshold: too low -> over-removed/too high -> duplicates remain (0.90 for paper)
Majority bias: mitigated by context bandit, stratified allocation, and deconfounded TS
Sample representativeness: explicitly characterize convenience samples, follow-up testing if necessary
Safety: Moderation API required, audit log of prompts and rejection criteria
Minimum recipe for implementation (for you)
Fixed battery + dynamic slot m available
Front: free writing → summary confirmation → grading matrix (own work + k cases)
Back: 5 embedded neighborhoods referenced in RAG → normalized questions in LLM → duplicate/toxicity filter → Q bank
Delivery: presentation probability update in GTS (indicators = importance/accuracy/encounter frequency, etc.)
Estimation: mean and difference with IPW, group heterogeneity with bandits that put attributes in context
summary

CSAS = "Participant Generated Questions x LLM Shaping x Bandit Optimization". This is a practical frame that picks up issues that are often overlooked in fixed questions in a short, dynamic, participatory manner.

Takahiro Yasuno

It has been a long time since my last post, but I am Takahiro Yasuno, a founding member of DD2030 (currently no longer a board member) and the leader of Team Mirai. Now that things have settled down a bit after the House of Councillors election, I would like to take this opportunity to greet and report to you once again, albeit belatedly.
[* Report of the Upper House activities on what was made in DD2030].

As a user of DD2030, I have made great use of some of the products developed by DD2030 in the Upper House election. I would like to report on some of the positive aspects and some areas that could be improved.
[* [Wide hearing AI]]
We used it in an attempt to include and visualize various textual data, such as X scraping data
It is easy to host, it can be run on a GUI, and I feel that it is becoming easier to use as software.
On the other hand, I had the impression that it was still in its infancy in terms of gaining insights that could be linked to actions.
Especially in the structuring of clustering, there are many places where I think it is still different as I read more, so I look forward to the development of the algorithm there.
Can we bridge the gap between human structuring and structuring by clustering?
