pages.title: Wage premium paid for less flexible hours of work

lines.text: Wage premium paid for less flexible hours of work
[wage premium] paid for [less flexible hours of work].
[Flexible working style]

>In Claudia Goldin's own Nobel Prize-winning study, "Why There Is a Gender Wage Gap," one of the main themes is that on-call response, or whether or not to respond to emergencies, creates a gender wage gap, which means women avoid being on call for emergency response.
fact-checking
[GPT5.icon]
Conclusion: The purpose is generally correct, but the wording is somewhat simplistic.

Goldin cites **a structure that pays a high premium to those who work long hours, specific hours, on-call support, and other forms of low time flexibility (= "greedy work" / low time flexibility)** as a major factor in the "residual" portion of the gender wage gap (the portion that cannot be explained by education, experience, or other factors). "greedy work" / low time flexibility)**. However, she does not explain this solely in terms of individual preferences, saying that women "avoid" being on-call, but rather that the uneven distribution of care responsibilities, such as childbirth and childcare, and the division of roles within couples influence decision-making. ([Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham https://paulgp.com/speeches/goldin_2014_aea.pdf])
Evidence (primary information and primary literature)
AER Paper (2014)

Goldin defines "workplace flexibility" as a multifaceted concept that includes not only the number of hours worked, but also specific time constraints, "on-call," face-to-face restraints, and customer service. It further argues that "the wage gap could be significantly reduced if there were no incentives to overly reward those who work long hours or specific time slots. It also states that "positions with 24/7 on-call will always remain," but that many jobs can be redesigned to lower the cost of flexibility. ([Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham https://paulgp.com/speeches/goldin_2014_aea.pdf])
Careers and Family: The Economics of Women's Lives.

The table of contents includes a chapter titled **"On Call "**, which suggests that on-call immediate response demands are at the heart of disparate job design. ([JSTOR https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctv1kbgt9p])

An excerpt from the same book (Harvard Gazette) also clearly states that the culprit of the modern wage gap is "greedy work" (long hours, non-linear compensation, and a premium for being able to respond at any time). Fairness within couples tends to be sacrificed and describes how men's and women's wages open up after the child-rearing years. ([Harvard Gazette https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2023/10/excerpt-from-career-and-family-by-claudia-goldin/])

*Various reviews and other sources also confirm that a Japanese translation was published by Keio University Press in 2023. ([www2.igs.ocha.ac.jp https://www2.igs.ocha.ac.jp/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/f16c145d6ad3d4fb8246a60d83a453d9.pdf?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
Nobel Prize related materials (2023)

The award was given for historical research on women's employment and earnings based on over 200 years of data. The recent disparity is attributed in part to **parenthood** and in part to the modern wage system, in which employers emphasize "uninterrupted career continuity" and time-based responsiveness, to the detriment of women. ([NobelPrize.org https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2023/press-release/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Where is the simplification?

It's not just about "on-call availability." At the core of Goldin is the design of **"nonlinear higher rewards for less flexible ways of working (long hours, specific hours, on-call, face-to-face restraints, etc.)**." ([Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham https://paulgp.com/speeches/goldin_2014_aea.pdf])

Rather than "women avoid it," "the structure makes it so." This explanation suggests that the burden of childbirth and childcare is unevenly distributed among women, and that as a result of domestic optimization, more women choose jobs and work styles with high time flexibility (but with low wage premiums), which cumulatively tend to create wage disparities. It is not reduced to a matter of individual "motivation" or "attitude. ([Harvard Gazette https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2023/10/excerpt-from-career-and-family-by-claudia-goldin/])

The disparity varies by job type. It is said that the disparity is greater in areas with strong nonlinear rewards, such as legal, finance, and corporate management, and that the disparity tends to narrow in areas that are well designed to substitute time (e.g., teaming, ease of handover, etc.). ([Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham https://paulgp.com/speeches/goldin_2014_aea.pdf])
Exact paraphrase (suggested)

>Goldin's argument is that most of today's gender wage gap is caused by the combination of a wage premium paid for "less flexible work hours," such as long hours, specific time slots, and on-call work, and the uneven distribution of the burden of care for childbirth and childcare. The disparity is not simply due to women "avoiding on-call," but rather to the structure of work design and the division of roles within the family, which facilitates the creation of the disparity. ([Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham https://paulgp.com/speeches/goldin_2014_aea.pdf])
Aside: Direction of solutions (Goldin's suggestion)

He argues that job design that **makes the wage/time relationship** more linear and lowers the cost of time flexibility (increased substitutability, teaming, institutionalized handover, etc.)** can help narrow the gap. ([Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham https://paulgp.com/speeches/goldin_2014_aea.pdf])
General Comments:

Your summary is right on in direction. However, when you say that the only main reason is the availability of on-call support or that women avoid it, you miss the point that Goldin emphasizes, which is the interaction between work design, compensation structure, and care responsibilities. Supplementing it with the above is more faithful to her point. ([Paul Goldsmith-Pinkham https://paulgp.com/speeches/goldin_2014_aea.pdf])

pages.title: Even without walking, creativity is enhanced by the perception of movement.

lines.text: Even without walking, creativity is enhanced by the perception of movement.

>[SFujita77 https://x.com/SFujita77/status/1972348302093111742] This sensationally reported 2014 study by Oppezzo & Schwartz of Stanford University, "Walking Enhances Ideation" but several methodological problems and interpretation biases have since been pointed out.
> Subsequent studies (e.g., Frith & Loprinzi 2018, Murali & Händel 2022) have continued to find no creativity improvement or that it can be explained by factors other than walking.

> In particular, creativity was enhanced just by watching "images of riding a moving train" in an experiment using VR by Fleury et al. et al. in 2020. → It is clear that the perception of motion and environmental stimuli are key, even without actually walking.
> Point
> ・The simple picture of walking = necessarily improved creativity is not supported by recent research.
> ・The presence or absence of effects depends on conditions (presence or absence of constraints, environmental stimuli, and type of task).
> ・The real factor is likely not "walking" but free body movement and sense of movement.
> Walking outside itself is healthy and I recommend it (laughs).
> >[AriyoshiMd https://x.com/AriyoshiMd/status/1972348302093111742] Walking around gets ideas?
> Stanford University Research
> ・When walking, ideas are more developed than when sitting.
> ・The inspiration effect continues for a while after walking
> ・Walking outdoors in particular, it is easier to come up with newer & higher quality ideas.
> ・"Go outside" alone is ineffective. It is important to actually walk.
> [https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G18wSKraIAAfLgY?format=jpg&name=medium#.png]
What's that? That's rather funny, isn't it?
[GPT5.icon]
Fact Check (Conclusion)

The claim is "partially correct," but the wording needs revision. Fleury et al.'s (2020) VR experiment showed that "simply perceiving a moving environment visually significantly increased [the range of ideas] (flexibility of divergent thinking)" without actually walking. However, creativity in general did not increase uniformly (no significant differences in other indices or convergence tasks). Also, it is an oversimplification to conclude that "environmental stimuli are the key" from this study alone. ([Rishi Vanukuru https://rishivanukuru.com/assets/documents/papers/tsc2020.pdf])
Rationale (contents of Fleury et al., 2020)

Condition: Participants created a "train cabin running in a tunnel" in immersive VR using an HMD and compared two conditions: stop vs. run (self-motion evoked by the movement of the train window). Participants performed creativity tasks (GAU = divergent, RAT = convergent). 32 participants. ([Rishi Vanukuru https://rishivanukuru.com/assets/documents/papers/tsc2020.pdf])

Results: Of the four GAU indicators, only flexibility significantly improved (t(29)=-2.140, p=0.041). **originality (p=0.087), fluency (p=0.135), and elaboration (p=0.415)** were not significantly different. Convergent tasks (RAT) were also not significantly different (p=0.489). Flexibility was higher in the running condition (9.07 for no movement to 12.81 for running), even in the mean, but the other results were not statistically confirmed. ([Rishi Vanukuru https://rishivanukuru.com/assets/documents/papers/tsc2020.pdf])

Implication: **The "expansion "** of ideas can be raised only by the perception of visual movement (sense of self-motion). However, it is too early to generalize "increased creativity" and the effect is index-limited. In addition, the sample is small in size, mainly young and VR-experienced students. ([Rishi Vanukuru https://rishivanukuru.com/assets/documents/papers/tsc2020.pdf])
Environmental Stimulation is Key"

This 2020 study does not go so far as to say that "environmental stimuli (e.g. nature/urban) are key" because the environment is unified in the train and only the presence of movement is manipulated. ([Rishi Vanukuru https://rishivanukuru.com/assets/documents/papers/tsc2020.pdf])

However, another Fleury et al. (2021) reported significantly higher creativity scores (especially novelty) when immersed in a natural landscape (forest) in a VR sketching task than in a black (no stimulus) or office environment, suggesting that "environmental stimuli contribute to creativity" independently.

On the other hand, the effect of walking itself, although not VR, is also robust. [Oppezzo & Schwartz 2014] show that walking, rather than outdoor movement stimuli alone (being pushed in a wheelchair), strongly boosts creative production, including up to Experiment 4. In other words, "environmental stimuli alone are not the key" and both physical movement and environment are likely involved.
Recommended modification of wording (more rigorous)

In an immersive VR experiment by Fleury et al. in 2020, simply presenting the visual self-motion of a "moving train" significantly increased **divergent thinking "flexibility "** compared to stop (no significant differences in other measures or convergence tasks). This suggests that the perception of movement can expand divergent thinking without the need to actually walk. Although this study alone cannot be definitive about environmental stimuli, there is another study in which VR of natural scenery enhanced creativity (especially novelty). ([Rishi Vanukuru https://rishivanukuru.com/assets/documents/papers/tsc2020.pdf])
In a word (TL;DR).
Positive: Simply showing a "running train" in VR significantly broadened the range of ideas.

Note: "Increased creativity overall" and "environmental stimuli alone are key" are overstatements. The effect is index-only, and the effect of the environment is supported by a separate study. The effect of walking itself is also strong. ([Rishi Vanukuru https://rishivanukuru.com/assets/documents/papers/tsc2020.pdf])

Primary source: Fleury et al. 2020 (Thinking Skills and Creativity)/Fleury et al. 2021 (ibid.)/Oppezzo & Schwartz, 2014 (JEP:LMC). ([Rishi Vanukuru https://rishivanukuru.com/assets/documents/papers/tsc2020.pdf])

pages.title: Osaka's prefectural assembly has reduced the number of councilors and increased the number of single-member wards.

lines.text: Osaka's prefectural assembly has reduced the number of councilors and increased the number of single-member wards.

>Many single-member wards were created in Osaka's prefectural assembly, forming an assembly in which the Restoration Association has an overwhelming majority, and the monopoly of political power by the Restoration Association has progressed.
fact-checking
[GPT5.icon]
Below is a fact check as of October 19, 2025. We have verified the claims in three categories.
Conclusion (summary)
1. "A number of one-person districts were created in the prefectural assembly."

→ Roughly true; as of 2019 (88), 31 of 53 districts are single-seat districts (about 58%), and 36 of 53 districts are single-seat districts (about 68%) under the new quorum of 79 starting with the 2023 elections. At least five electoral districts have been changed from two-person to one-person districts. ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170030/gikai_giji/kaikaku/teisuu-hyou.html])
2. "A congress with an overwhelming majority was formed by the Restoration Association."

→ The "single majority (approx. 65%)" is true in terms of numbers. The current factional composition is 51 Ishin/79, which is approximately 65%. However, it has not reached 2/3 (= 53 seats) by itself. ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170010/gikai_giji/giininfo/kaihakousei20.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. "The monopoly of political power by the Restoration has progressed."

→ This is an expression of evaluation (opinion). As a matter of fact, the Restoration has a majority in the prefectural assembly, the governor is also a Restoration member (to be reelected in 2023), and the Osaka City Assembly has the largest number of Restoration members (46/81)**, confirming a situation in which political influence has become increasingly concentrated. However, this is not a situation that can legally be called a "monopoly" (e.g., more than two-thirds on its own). ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Osaka_gubernatorial_election?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Rationale Details
(i) One-person districts have actually increased

As of 2019 (at the time of the 2019 election), 31 of the 53 electoral districts are "one" on the official list. ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170030/gikai_giji/kaikaku/teisuu-hyou.html])
In the official list after the 2023 election, 36 of the 53 constituencies are "one person". ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170030/gikai_giji/kaikaku/senkyoku0504.html])

The number of members will be revised from 88 to 79 by ordinance in March 2022. The revision includes Sumiyoshi Ward, Sakai Ward, Sakai Kita Ward, Izumiotsu, Takaishi, and Senboku Counties, and Minoh and Toyono-Gun, etc. to **"2 to 1"** (There are also reductions from 4 to 3, 3 to 2, and 5 to 4). ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170030/gikai_giji/kaikaku/teisusinn.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
The above indicates that the number of one-person districts has actually increased (from 31 to 36)**, although the expression "a large number of new one-person districts" is a bit exaggerated.

Note: Regarding the background of the reduction in the number of seats, the press reports that it was initiated by the Restoration Association and passed with the approval of the Liberal Democratic Party, New Kōmeitō, and others (background explanation). ([Mainichi https://mainichi.jp/articles/20230315/ddn/041/010/020000c?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(2) Restoration seats (an "overwhelming majority"?)

The latest composition of the Osaka Prefectural Assembly (as of August 15, 2025) is: Restoration 51, New Komeito 14, LDP 6, and a few others. With a quorum of 79 (1 vacancy), the Restoration Party has the sole majority. However, since it has not reached two-thirds (53), it is not in a position to pass bills that require a special majority by itself. ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170010/gikai_giji/giininfo/kaihakousei20.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(iii) Facts about "monopoly of power
Governor: Hirofumi Yoshimura (Restoration) re-elected on April 9, 2023. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Osaka_gubernatorial_election?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Osaka City Council: Restoration 46/81 in the 2023 municipal election.([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Osaka_City_Council_election?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

In light of the above, the evaluation that the "concentration of power has progressed" is valid, as the system in which the Restoration has strong influence in the executive branch (governor) plus the main assemblies (prefectural assembly and city assembly) has continued. However, it should be noted that "monopoly" is a value judgment and not a monopoly by definition (more than two-thirds alone). ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Osaka_gubernatorial_election?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Summary (Judgment)

Fact: The number of single-seat constituencies increased (from 31 to 36) along with a reduction in the number of seats (from 88 to 79). Restoration has a single-seat majority (51/79 ≈ 65%). ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170030/gikai_giji/kaikaku/teisusinn.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Evaluation: "Monopoly" is a strong expression. While there is certainly a concentration of influence, it is **legally and numerically "less than 2/3 alone "**, and it is inaccurate to assert that it is a complete monopoly. ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170010/gikai_giji/giininfo/kaihakousei20.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If necessary, I can show you a full list of single-member districts/multiple-member districts and their ratios, or chart how the seats have moved from 2019 to 2023.
[nishio.icon]What happened in the elections before the capacity reduction?
[GPT5.icon]
In a nutshell - **before the capacity reduction (2019, 88 seats, 53 districts)** it was like this.

Two-person wards: 15, three-person wards: 2, four-person wards: 4, five-person wards: 1 (=Higashi-Osaka City).

Increase in single-seat constituencies: 31 → 36 (out of 53 constituencies, approx. 58.5% → approx. 67.9%) ([Osaka Prefectural Government https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/o170030/gikai_giji/kaikaku/teisuu-hyou.html])

pages.title: Proportional representation is designed to reflect minority voices in the House.

lines.text: Proportional representation is designed to reflect minority voices in the House.
>[ysw31120588 https://x.com/ysw31120588/status/1979749741098627243] Many of you have posted about the issue of reducing the number of members of the Restoration Council,
> To begin with, I feel that I am wrong in my premise.
> Proportional representation is a system created to prevent "runaway majority rule.
> In nineteenth-century Europe, the forces that won the primary elections monopolized the parliament and the voices of the minority disappeared.
> For example, even if a party receives 40% of the total vote, it will only receive first place, which means that some parties will have no seats.
> The proportional representation system was born out of this reflection, with the idea of allocating seats in accordance with the percentage of votes received.
> In other words, proportionality is a device to protect the diversity of democracy.
> But the current "reduction in the number of Diet members" is in effect a reduction in the number of proportional quotas.
> It appears to "reduce waste" but actually "reduces the breadth of public opinion.
> As a result, the center and the major parties become stronger and bureaucratic control deepens.
> What needs real reform is not the number of seats, but the design of the electoral system.
> For example, revising the constituency system and a mechanism to finance elections with government bonds.
> Such "[public investment that supports democracy]" is the original political reform.
fact-checking
[GPT5.icon]
Conclusion (summary)

The purpose of [proportional representation]: "to reduce the bias of seats toward the majority and to reflect the voices of the [minority] in the seats" - a generally correct general explanation, and consistent with the fact that PR (proportional representation) was introduced successively in many European countries in the late 19th and early 20th centuries (e.g. Belgium introduced PR in national politics in 1899). (e.g., Belgium introduced PR in the national government in 1899). ([Encyclopedia Britannica https://www.britannica.com/summary/proportional-representation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Proportional representation is a device to prevent "majority rule run amok" - generally accurate.

Proportional representation (PR) allocates seats according to the percentage of votes received, a system that makes it easier to ensure minority representation. PR was introduced in Europe from the mid-19th century to the early 20th century, and its adoption expanded in response to the distortions of majority representation (discrepancy between votes received and seats). [Belgium] is often cited as the earliest example of the introduction of PR in a national government in 1899. ([Encyclopedia Britannica https://www.britannica.com/summary/proportional-representation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
"19th century European constituencies = vanishing minorities" - valid as a point of trend.

It is a settled theory in political science that the majority representation system of the time gave seat bonuses to the large parties and tended to underrepresent minority parties. The history of the introduction of PR in Belgium and other countries was also based on the correction of these distortions. ([Cambridge University Press & Assessment https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-political-science-review/article/when- dominant-parties-adopt-proportional-representation-the-mysterious-case-of-belgium/839A8A29F0DFE16109F559552BA8A9B5?utm_source= chatgpt.com])

'Zero seats can happen even with 40% of the vote': institutionally correct (zero seats if always second in each constituency); standard knowledge is that constituency/quota-centric systems such as FPTP/SMD and SNTV are prone to discrepancies between votes and seats (in the UK 2015 general election UKIP had 12.6% of the vote nationwide, one seat etc.). ([ACE Electoral Knowledge Network https://aceproject.org/ace-en/topics/es/esd/esd01/esd01a/esd01a01/mobile_browsing/onePag?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
It is possible to get 40% of the vote and still have no seats in the House" - true under the system (but a theoretical extreme)

In single-winner constituencies (constituencies), only the first place in each ward is elected, so even if you get 40% nationally, if you are second in each ward, zero seats are theoretically possible. In real life examples, a large discrepancy between votes and seats occurred in the UK 2015, with UKIP getting 12.6% and only 1/650 of the seats. ([ACE Electoral Knowledge Network https://aceproject.org/ace-en/topics/es/esd/esd01/esd01a/esd01a01/mobile_browsing/onePag?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
'Reduces the breadth of popular opinion/ Makes the major parties stronger.'

As a matter of fact, the smaller the number of districts (m), the higher the effective threshold required to be elected, and the harder it is for small parties and minorities to gain seats (basic theory of electoral systems). The general proposition that the change from multiple districts to single-seat districts is in the direction of reducing proportionality is valid. ([ACE Electoral Knowledge Network https://aceproject.org/main/english/es/esg04.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
However, **"deepening bureaucratic control" is a causal claim** and no verifiable concrete evidence is provided (area of evaluation and opinion).
The first half is valid as a general theory, the second half is an evaluation.

Theoretical and empirical studies: the smaller the number of electoral districts (M), the higher the percentage of votes needed to win the election = disadvantageous to small parties and less proportionality; single-seat constituencies tend to reduce the proportionality of seat allocation and work to the advantage of large parties - standard international knowledge. ([ACE Electoral Knowledge Network https://aceproject.org/main/english/es/esg04.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Bureaucratic control" is a value judgment, as no demonstration directly linked to institutional change has been presented.
The design of the electoral system is the main issue/ the proposal to finance the election with government bonds" → The former is an opinion, the latter is different from the current system.

The institutional design emphasis is a policy proposal (opinion). Specific measures include MMP (constituency + proportional linkage), STV, and a variety of other design options. ([Idea https://www.idea.int/sites/default/files/publications/mixed-electoral-system-design-and-pratice.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Election financing in Japan: Under current law, part of the election campaign is paid for out of tax revenue through "public financing of election (public expenditure)". The system of financing with government bonds (debt) has not been generalized (even in the information provided by local governments and election authorities, public expense sharing is explained as a budgetary measure). ([City of Tottori https://www.city.tottori.lg.jp/www/contents/1758171985243/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Selection and Arrangement
[selection] and [array (programming, programing)
[文章を書く]ということは選択と配列である、的なことを [Jiro Kawakita] か [Tadao Umesao] がいってなかったっけ[nishio.icon]
[GPT5.icon]

It is true that we often see the phrase "editing (i.e., writing) is a matter of 'selection' and 'arrangement,'" but we cannot find a source for this phrase as a strictly stylized phrase by Jiro Kawakita or Tadao Umesao.
However, the idea of proximity is strong on both sides.

Tadao Umesao consistently emphasizes the importance of sorting by cards and "[knee-swing (gymnastics)]" around "[The Art of Intellectual Production]", and the famous phrase [* "[Don't classify, arrange]"] has been circulating. The phrase is also used as an institutional source. Even as an institutional source, the phrase is cited in the research repository materials of the National Museum of Ethnology. ([ir.soken.ac.jp https://ir.soken.ac.jp/record/2250/files/3-18_Minpaku_Mihara_A5.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Jiro Kawakita ([KJ method]) proceeds with [selection] and [configuration] (arrangement) of materials step by step by carding disparate fragments, grouping them by similarity (sorting), relating them, illustrating them, and writing about them. Although we cannot find any evidence of "selection and arrangement" as his formulaic phrase, the content of the methodology is exactly that. ([Web site to support process innovation and problem solving in the manufacturing industry (monozukuri.com) https://www.monodukuri.com/gihou/article/1824?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

In addition, the Japanese Copyright Law defines an "edited work" as "one that has creativity through the selection or arrangement of materials." This phrase derived from the law is behind the general expression "editing = selection and arrangement. From here, it tends to be diverted as the essence of writing and editing in general. ([jfpi.or.jp https://www.jfpi.or.jp/webyogo/index.php?term=4380&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Conclusion.

The phrase "writing is a process of selection and arrangement" is a "common summary" that was born from the combination of Umesao's emphasis on "arrangement" and the practice of KJ method, and the terminology of "selection and arrangement" in copyright law. Rather than attributing it to a person's name with a strict source, I think it is safer to explain that "Umesao emphasized "arrangement" and Kawakita's KJ method is also a practical technique of "selection -> arrangement"". ([ir.soken.ac.jp https://ir.soken.ac.jp/record/2250/files/3-18_Minpaku_Mihara_A5.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If you want to write with sources, for example:

The writing process consists of (1) selection of materials and (2) organization (arrangement). Tadao Umesao emphasized the significance of arrangement in his "The Art of Intellectual Production," saying, "Don't classify, arrange." Jiro Kawakita's KJ method is a technique for proceeding from card selection and grouping to arrangement, illustration, and writing. ). ([ir.soken.ac.jp https://ir.soken.ac.jp/record/2250/files/3-18_Minpaku_Mihara_A5.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

What if I put only high YouTube ratings on Sensemaker?
We can get high rating data from YouTube, but not low rating data.
What would happen if only highly rated data were included in the poll?
[Claude.icon]
If only the YouTube-derived high ratings are included in the voting result data as affirmative votes, the processing flow will be as follows:
1. data loading stage (runner_utils.ts: lines 347-365)
The getVoteInfoFromCsvRow function converts CSV data into a VoteTally object:
code:ts
return new VoteTally(Number(row["agrees"]), Number(row["disagrees"]), Number(row["passes"]));
For YouTube-derived data:
agrees = number of high ratings
disagrees = 0 (or blank -> NaN, so be careful)
passes = 0 (or blank -> NaN, so be careful)
2. statistical calculation stage (stats/stats_util.ts)
Treat undefined values as 0 with passCount || 0 when calculating the vote percentage:

} else {
return (voteTally.passCount || 0) / totalCount;
In YouTube-derived data:
Percentage in favor ≈ 100% (if there is a high rating)
Opposition ≈ 0
Pass rate ≈ 0

code:ts
this.filteredComments = comments.filter(isCommentWithVoteInfoType).filter((comment) => {
return getCommentVoteCount(comment, true) >= this.minVoteCount;
Important: minVoteCount = 20, so comments with less than 20 high ratings are excluded from the analysis.
This is not good.[nishio.icon]

(comment) => this.getCommonGroundAgreeScore(comment),
k,

minCommonGroundProb = 0.7 (70%) is the threshold value. almost all YouTube-derived comments with high ratings are extracted as Common Ground, since the approval rate is almost 100%. Comments with the highest number of high ratings are given priority.
5. extraction of Differences of Opinion (majority_vote.ts: lines 189-210)

// ... Similar conditions apply to the DISAGREE RATE

Topic Extraction → Classification with LLM
[nishio.icon]
[Talk to the City Turbo] and Google [Jigsaw Sensemaker] share a common mechanism for extracting topics from text using LLM and then classifying which topic each comment is about.
Which is original or have a common ancestor?
[GPT5.icon]

Just a conclusion first: Based on public information, the "mechanism (topic extraction with LLM -> multi-label classification of each utterance)" is a general pattern that both arrived at independently, and there is no evidence that one is derived from the other. Looking only at the timeline of project release, the Talk to the City (TttC) main body preceded the Jigsaw Sensemaker OSS, and the Jigsaw Sensemaker OSS followed. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/talk-to-the-city-an-open-source-ai-tool-to- scale-deliberation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
rough timeline

2023-10-25: TttC published on its blog the process of "extracting claims -> clustering similar claims (topics/sub-topics)" in LLM. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/talk-to-the-city-an-open-source-ai-tool-to- scale-deliberation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Around 2025-01: Jigsaw published a library including "Topic Identification / Statement Categorization" on Sensemaker's GitHub (first issue was 1/9). ([GitHub https://github.com/Jigsaw-Code/sensemaking-tools])

2025-02: First Sensemaker in operation in the City of Bowling Green (media stated "introduced in February"). ([adweek.com https://www.adweek.com/media/not-all-ai-is-for-profit-meet-googles-civic-tech-experiment/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

2025-04: Sensemaker case study article reported in various places. ([techbrew.com https://www.techbrew.com/stories/2025/04/22/bowling-green-kentucky-ai-tool-google-jigsaw-sensemaker?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
Specify the "mechanism" of each

TttC/Turbo: The guide clearly states that the "Cluster Extraction" node creates topics / subtopics and combines them with OpenAI keys to form a pipeline. ([talktothecity.org https://talktothecity.org/docs/ai-pipe-guide])

Sensemaker: README clearly describes Topic Identification and Statement Categorization (Vertex AI/Gemini implementation, schema constrained decoding, etc.). ([GitHub https://github.com/Jigsaw-Code/sensemaking-tools])
What about "common ancestor?"

Rather than a specific project-derived "ancestor," it is reasonable to conclude that a generalized topic extraction/classification design using LLM as an annotator spread in 2023-24, to which the Polis-based conversation mapping lineage was connected (Jigsaw also announced its collaboration with Polis). The research literature also shows examples of LLM-based topic extraction pipelines in 2024. ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/what-could-bg-be-enabling-a-large-scale-conversation-in-kentucky-70071f4fe268?utm_source=chatgpt .com])

In short: convergent evolution rather than original conflict. In terms of release date, "TttC (October 2023 release description, not 2013) is first" and "Sensemaker's OSS release is early 2025", in that order. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/talk-to-the-city-an-open-source-ai-tool-to- scale-deliberation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

pages.title: How to handle .ipynb in Claude Code

lines.text: How to handle .ipynb in Claude Code
[GPT5.icon]
A "good way" to handle .ipynb in Claude Code

Conclusion: If you value stability and reproducibility, pair with `.py:percent` in Jupytext -> let Claude Code edit `.py` and update `.ipynb` in sync. Direct editing of notes is possible, but there are reports of cell order bugs, so it is safer to use MCP server together or via Jupytext. ([Anthropic https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-best-practices?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
1) Let the notes be read as is and lightly edited (for small scale)

Open `.ipynb` in VS Code and have Claude Code read the contents by file reference (e.g. `@notebooks/analysis.ipynb`). Instruct the user to go to the cell list, edit only the relevant cell, and apply the patch in this order. ([Anthropic https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-best-practices?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Note: There are reports of edits not being reflected/cell order being corrupted. Avoid heavy work. ([Reddit https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeCode/comments/1mwd2qj/claude_code_and_jupyter_notebooks_in_vscode/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
This, this, this, this, they're going to shove the cells in reverse order.[nishio.icon]
Noise reduction (highly recommended)
code:bash
# Clear output once (to prevent token pressure with huge base64 images)
jupyter nbconvert --clear-output --inplace your.ipynb
([Stack Overflow https://stackoverflow.com/questions/17077494/how-do-i-convert-a-ipython-notebook-into-a-python-file-via-commandline?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2) Pair .ipynb⇄.py in Jupytext (most recommended)
Claude Code is good at editing scripts. Sync `.ipynb` with `.py:percent` format and let Claude edit `.py`. Update notes in sync after completion.
code:bash
pipx install jupytext nbconvert nbstripout
# pair ipynb with py:percent
jupytext --set-formats ipynb,py:percent your.ipynb
# Bidirectional synchronization after editing thereafter
jupytext --sync your.ipynb
# Always delete extraneous output (optional)
nbstripout --install
([jupytext.readthedocs.io https://jupytext.readthedocs.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
point

`.py:percent` has explicit cell borders (`# %%`) and is strong for difference management. ([jupytext.readthedocs.io https://jupytext.readthedocs.io/en/latest/formats-scripts.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Only **.py` is passed to Claude for editing -> reflected in `.ipynb` with `jupytext --sync`.
Most stable for large notes/repetitive renovations.
3) Cell-by-cell operation on MCP server (with Claude Desktop)

Claude (especially Claude Desktop) can be integrated with external tools via MCP; by adding an MCP server for Jupyter, cell enumeration, reading, editing, etc. of notes can be performed securely as tools.
Typical example:.
`UsamaK98/python-notebook-mcp` (provides cell add/edit/read tools) ([GitHub https://github.com/UsamaK98/python-notebook-mcp])
`datalayer/jupyter-mcp-server` (supports various MCP clients) ([GitHub https://github.com/datalayer/jupyter-mcp-server?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Introduction image (excerpt):.
code:bash
git clone https://github.com/UsamaK98/python-notebook-mcp
cd python-notebook-mcp
uv venv && uv pip install -r requirements.txt
fastmcp install server.py --name "Jupyter Notebook MCP"
# Enabled in Developer settings in Claude Desktop

(MCP is a standard protocol published by Anthropic that works well with the Claude product line) ([The Verge https://www.theverge.com/2024/11/25/24305774/anthropic-model-context-protocol -data-sources?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Prompt/Operational Tips
Editing is done by "Cell Specific -> Patch". Example.
Output the list of cells in `@analysis.ipynb` by number/type/first line → change only the cell to be written as "preprocess" → explain the difference of the change → apply.
The huge output is removed in advance (`nbconvert --clear-output` above) and the images are made into external files for reference.
Specify that fragile metadata (such as `cell_id`) is not to be touched.
Jupytext group has made it a habit to review on the `.py` side -> `--sync` to finalize.

Four Broad Listening Data Types
There are four main forms of broad listening data
However, the world's understanding of data structures, especially for new systems, is still limited, so they are often confused with conventional data types (≒questionnaires).
Summary image
[https://gyazo.com/4575b88c1ea56b9da058b0fa1ed16087]
[*** [Polis type]]
[https://gyazo.com/22e55affa2df0599cd2273513ef018ff]
Data on K statements for which N people voted for, against, or neutral.
It takes the form of a matrix of four different values, including missing values, also called a [vote matrix].
Famous examples include Taiwan's decade of digital democracy and the recent case of [bowling green
[*** [interview type]]
[https://gyazo.com/809c49607caedc24a8404bf07bd98548]
Data on N people, each of whom was interacted with by the interviewer to elicit information.
Before LLM, the cost of interviewers was too high to be used on a large scale, but LLM has made "AI interviewers" feasible and expanded their applications.

The [IIDOBATA system] developed as part of the [Digital Democracy 2030] project was applied to Team Mirai's [Talkable Manifesto] for the 2025 Upper House election, leading to the collection of 20,000 problem awareness data.
I wrote about this story in "[Findings from Team Mirai's social experiment "Talkable Manifesto"].
[Findings from Team Mirai's social experiment "Talkable Manifesto"｜NISHIO Hirokazu https://note.com/nishiohirokazu/n/nb35e8d526fd4?sub_rt=share_pb]
[*** Choice Questionnaire Type]
[https://gyazo.com/2b4f88c964c4afec4977ce6242d9295c]
Widely practiced before the LLM, "how to gather information from the masses."
Election voting is included in this in a broad sense.

Because of the ease of tabulation without LLMs, it became the de facto standard in the pre-LLM world to quantitatively tabulate this type of questionnaire and to do [majority rule] in election voting.
It has been pointed out that majority voting is problematic as a method of tallying votes. Explained in books such as "[Doubt the majority vote.

There was an argument that "this kind of [quantitative study] alone is not enough, [qualitative study] is important," but the cost of qualitative research was too high to be carried out on a large scale.
[*** open-ended questionnaire type].
The free-text field was added as a result of trying to somehow pick up information that was not picked up by the "choice questionnaire" before the LLM
but how to analyze what was written there has long been a major challenge
Natural language processing such as [word frequency analysis] and [topic extraction] have been studied
The advent of LLM has made analysis much easier.
This was utilized in 2023 [Talk to the City].
Wide hearing AI also assumes this data type.
[*** About Polis type]
Polis type can be regarded as a choice questionnaire type
Therefore, any multiple-choice questionnaire can be regarded as [Polis type data] and analyzed in a Polis-like manner.
[Polis-like visualization of the 2022 House of Councillors election] : There are 42 5-step questions and 592 politicians answered, so it is a matrix visualization of (592, 42) dimensions
If you use the actual Polis system, respondents can add questions (can be turned on or off by settings).
This is where we differ from traditional surveys.
Opinions not picked up in the optional questionnaire can also be picked up as in the open-ended questionnaire.
In other words, it can be seen as a hybrid of the two types of surveys.
This free-text submission will be an optional survey question item.
This can be seen as a solution to the [open question is hard to answer] problem.
While answering easy-to-answer multiple-choice questions, your opinions are organized and then submitted as additional opinions when they are not fully output in the multiple-choice answers.

On the other hand, organizing and writing one's opinion in a single text field is a difficult task for most people, and often incomplete (others cannot understand or vote on the content based on the posted text string alone) submissions are made.
[*** About the interview type]
AI interviewers are a solution to this problem of "difficulty in organizing and writing opinions in a single text field without excesses or deficiencies.
In other words, the AI will ask for the information it needs, organize it, and submit it
To ensure a homogeneous AI of submitters, writing in the prompts what you would like to see submitted will provide granular data even from conversations with different people.

Conceptually open grammatical closed questions
Grammatical [closed question] open conceptually

>"Is it right to lie?" is considered a closed question. However, what is important is that it is conceptually open. The initial "yes"/"no" answer to this question is the questioner's "Why do you think so?" "Could it be otherwise?" can be made "open" by the questioner's "Why do you think so?" and "Could it be otherwise?" which can encourage detailed explanation and exploration.
from [open question is hard to answer].
[Open question - Wikipedia https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%83%97%E3%83%B3%E3%82%AF%E3%82%A8%E3%82%B9%E3%83%81%E3%83% A7%E3%83%B3]

>In educational settings, [open questions] are generally considered "good" questions. Open questions result in longer responses that allow students to demonstrate their understanding. Open questions are considered preferable to closed questions in this regard because they are more appropriate for discussion and exploration, whereas closed questions (questions that require a "yes"/"no" response) are only appropriate for testing.

> [Peter Worley] argues that this is a false assumption. This is based on Worley's central argument that there are two different kinds of open and closed questions: grammatical and conceptual. He argues that educators should aim for questions that are "grammatically closed but conceptually open." For example, in standard parlance, "Is it right to lie?" would be considered a closed question. However, what is important is that it is conceptually open. The initial "yes"/"no" answer to this question is the questioner's "Why do you think so?" "Could it be otherwise?" can be made "open" by the questioner's "Why do you think so?" and "Could it be otherwise?" which can encourage detailed explanation and exploration.

> This grammatically closed but conceptually open question style offers educators the best of both worlds. It combines the "focus" and "specificity" of closed questions (which is, after all, why teachers use closed questions) with the dual benefits of "invitation" and "detail" of open questions, Worley argues. Closed questions simply require a strategy for "opening up" in order to ensure that conceptually open questions can fulfill their pedagogical potential.

> Worley's structural and semantic differences between open-ended and closed questions are integral to his educational invention, "[the] Open Questioning Mindset (OQM)," which refers to educators developing an open attitude toward the learning process and the questions at its heart. It is a concept that can be applied to all subjects and all educational environments. Teachers who develop an open questioning mindset listen openly to the cognitive content of student statements and look for ways to use what is given as an opportunity for learning, regardless of whether it is right or wrong, or appears to be relevant or irrelevant. oQM encourages a teaching style that emphasizes authentic inquiry in the classroom. Encouraging a teaching style that emphasizes what Worley calls "guess what's in my head," OQM provides teachers with the tools to move beyond a closed, guided questioning approach to teaching.

pages.title: Balancing Selfishness and Altruism in OSS Quest

lines.text: Balancing Selfishness and Altruism in OSS Quest
from  [OSS Quest]
Balancing [self-interest] and [altruism] in OSS quests
[code4japan slack]
Shingo OHKI

>If you start a small project (like engineer: 5, copywriter: 3) by yourself and complete it all by yourself in one turn, you can make a move to get all the contribution points, which seems like a strategy for this game (contrary to the values of the game?). (Is this contrary to the values of the game?) There are times when this is the strategy of the game. However, in the end, someone other than the person who made that move won.
nishio
This simply means that if you do your own project, it is a +4 contribution, but if you do someone else's, it is a +5 contribution, so it is inefficient.

Since creating a project in the first place is two actions for four points, it is less than half as efficient as advancing a project, and it is more efficient to help others around with their projects without creating your own project.
Of course, if no one creates a project, no one can contribute, so eventually it becomes necessary to start a project, albeit a little inefficiently.
I feel like this is a really good understanding of OSS.

Many people think of "contributing to a project" as contribution, but it is also an act that consumes resources called "contribution opportunities. which may be a bit of a hassle and offer little return.
I think this is well represented as a trade-off in the game.

I see, "starting a project" is 4 points for 2 actions and contribution is 8~10 points for 2 actions, so projects that are completed in the short term are less efficient in scoring points in the first place. You'd misinterpret it as a good means of scoring points because you get points right away in the short term, but in fact, long-term projects are more efficient in scoring points, so even if you're ahead in small projects, you'll get swept up in the second half of the project.
Well done!

pages.title: Without training, older ASDs will be cut off.

lines.text: Without training, older ASDs will be cut off.

>[toshio_t_44 https://x.com/toshio_t_44/status/1982348319310623226] It sounds cruel, but that doesn't mean that older ASDs will be cut off if they are not trained to adapt. What has happened in recent years, as knowledge about ASD has become more prevalent in the general public, is that, first, the younger generation is getting trained in rehabilitation at an early age. Also, people in the gray zone who are making efforts and adapting to society become more aware that they have ASD elements. Then, ASD in the wild, who left their characteristics untrained, will be seen as [self-responsible] because they [failed to make the necessary effort].

> This is just a feeling, but when I look at new graduate hires in recent years at companies above that level, I feel that I no longer see the obvious high-intelligent ASD types that were a certain number a long time ago. I suspect this is a combination of the fact that, as a result of the spread of knowledge about ASD, people with the trait are now receiving early rehabilitation and mimicking the stereotypes, and that ASD in the wild are now being actively eliminated.

> >MaybeAsd5963: There aren't many institutions that can provide specialized communication training for people who discover they have Aspies as adults. Even self-help groups are hard to find. x.com/toshio_t_44/st...
[GPT5.icon]
That is a strong assertion. Since there is a mixture of facts, experiences, and norms, I will isolate the main points and comment on them.
1) Factual part
Masking/Camouflage

Behaviors in which individuals on the autism spectrum hide or compensate for their traits to avoid disadvantages in society are widely reported, especially in adults (higher in women). It is also associated with the burden of depression, anxiety, and burnout. ([PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27899710/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Effectiveness of early support (rehabilitation)

While small to moderate improvements in adaptive behavior, IQ, etc. have been shown with Early Intensive Behavioral Intervention (EIBI) and other programs, the evidence is not strong enough to generalize to "mimicking the stereotypes and becoming invisible" (and the summary that the effects are limited). ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6494600/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2) What you can see/not see in the data
The number of "obvious high-intelligence ASD types" among new graduates has decreased.

There are no statistics that directly indicate this. Conversely, on a macro level, employment of persons with disabilities in Japan is on the rise, with both the number and actual employment rate of persons with disabilities in the private sector at record highs in 2024, including a +15.7%** increase in **mental disabilities (including developmental disabilities) over the previous year. This is not consistent with the generalization of "active exclusion" (even the breakdown between general and disability quotas is a separate issue). ([Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/newpage_47084.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3) Normative and institutional aspects (Is "cut off at one's own risk" appropriate?)

In Japan, "provision of reasonable accommodation" by business operators is obligatory after 2024/4/1. Unreasonable discriminatory treatment on the basis of disability is prohibited, and failure to provide consideration (even though it is not overburdening) is a problem. In other words, "cutting down" is neither ethically nor legally acceptable. ([Cabinet Office website https://www8.cao.go.jp/shougai/suishin/sabekai_leaflet-r05.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
4) Language and Framing

**Expressions such as "ASD in the wild" or "high IQ ASD type "** reinforce the stigma. As a matter of fact, it is more constructive to rephrase them as "undiagnosed/unsupported ASD" or "high IQ parties".

Emphasizing only "training to adapt" tends to increase the masking load. It is more sustainable to simultaneously promote universal design/reasonable considerations on the selection/work environment side (e.g., shared pre-questioning, written selection options, sensory stimulation considerations, trial task-based evaluation, clear work rules). ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5509825/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
5) If you want to verify this claim
(A) Percentage of ASD parties over time in the general quota for new graduates vs. the quota for persons with disabilities.
(B) Comparison of camouflage scale (e.g., CAT-Q) distributions among the same generation
(C) Tracking of Early Assistance Receipt History and Employment Outcomes
-- is needed. At this time, the evidence for extending individual experience to society-wide trends is weak. ([PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30361940/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Conclusion:

The linear narrative of "medical treatment and education mimics the stereotype → wildness is self-imposed and eliminated" is not adequately supported by either evidence or the legal system. It is more realistic to read that what is becoming less visible is a combination of (1) increased masking and support, (2) diversification of recruitment channels (e.g., disability quotas, job-specific hiring), and (3) labeling issues. ([PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34563942/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

community ethics

>[D6f8Z https://x.com/D6f8Z/status/1982348219481985185] ... Today's old people are the ones who caused the collapse of communal ethics in the postwar democracy, so they are being countered by the younger generation with "don't take away communal logic when it suits you," and from there the foundations of the nation-state are shaking.
> We are probably seeing the beginning of the end of the modern state.
> >takasugi_mbsjk: To begin with, the modern state is based on the social contract theory foundation of "protecting the life and health of all citizens.

> "Reducing benefits to protect fiscal sustainability" is frequently argued, but when the argument drifts in the direction of "reducing one's own burden by cutting others' health care," it leads to a breakdown of communal ethics.
[GPT5.icon]
Copy. We will break the claim down into its elements and consider it short.
decomposition of an argument
1. causal claim: The "Mere Old Man" = the entity that caused the "collapse of communal ethics" under the postwar democracy.
2. rebuttal claim: the generation below counters with **"Don't take away from the community theory only when it's convenient. "**.
3. consequential assertion: the repartee shakes the foundation of the nation-state.
Steelman (enhanced interpretation)

Postwar "corporate community" → dismantled by job mobility since the 1990s. Requiring young people to provide pro bono service (neighborhood association/PTA-like obligations) to the community community after retirement will cause a backlash as a **lack of consistency (time inconsistency of preferences)**.

When the asymmetry of intergenerational redistribution of pensions and healthcare (which can easily appear skewed toward the elderly due to demographic changes) is justified on the basis of "community," the sense of belonging and trust among the younger generation declines → institutional legitimacy (the "foundation") is worn away.
Weaknesses and leaps in logic

Over-identification of the main cause: The primary causes of the collapse are structural factors such as urbanization, higher education, declining birthrates, female employment, globalization, and technological change. To determine a specific generation as the "cause" is an over-identification of causal attribution.

Duality of community: liberation from the pre-modern "family and land" bondage = expansion of rights as well. If we view disintegration simply as a bad thing, we miss the diversity of normative preferences.
Unclear what "shaky foundations" really means: Foundations = financial sustainability? Social trust? Tax compliance? Security? -Need to identify indicators.
Operational definitions and validation hypotheses (measurable form)
Community ethics = defined as "free and semi-compulsory mutual aid expectations.
Draft indicators: neighborhood association membership, community volunteer hours, PTA participation, and out-of-office network density (by cohort).
Intergenerational backlash = "resistance to communitarianism"
Indicators: refusal of young people to "mobilize for free," perceived legitimacy of taxes and social insurance premiums.
I see.[nishio.icon]
Is the norm that "[free mobilization] is exploitative and evil" becoming stronger and clashing with those who believe that "free mobilization is natural?"
Foundation" = Institutional Trust and Belonging
Draft indicators: government and municipal trust, taxpayer norms, voter turnout (especially among young people), and social trust in general.
→ Hypothesis H1: Younger people are more likely to consider the "private burden of community obligations" to be unjust and have less trust in the system.
→ Hypothesis H2: Designing **symmetrical reciprocity (visualization of give & take)** in the community will restore participation of young people.
Alternative Framing
It is not "the old man broke it," but rather an externality that accompanies the institutional shift from corporate community to individualization.
The challenge is **"re-bundling the norm "**: how to redistribute the mutual assistance that was carried out by the house/company, with autonomy, market, state, and digital infrastructure.
Implications (Practical)
Symmetry design: time bank, micro remuneration, and future credit (postpaid reciprocity) are introduced for regional tasks.
Cross-generational visibility: dashboard of who is responsible for how much (opacity creates "don't take").
Re-contracting of rights/obligations: The allocation of pensions, long-term care, and education is discussed in intergenerational "double-entry bookkeeping" (both benefits and burdens are indicated).
Multi-layered small communities: Diversify the risk of dependence through "multi-layered belonging" by layering communities of interest x local ties x online, rather than a single leg of local ties.
Digital deliberation: UI/participation design (asynchronous, short time, reporting automation) to reduce the burden on young people (time and disposable income).
summary

While the proposition includes the insight of inequity among young people → declining institutional trust, there is a strong bias toward generational mono-causality. A redesign that is centered on structural factors but satisfies symmetry of reciprocity, visibility, and diversity of preferences is appropriate as a solution.

Brahmin Leftists
[GPT5.icon]

The Brahmin Left is a term used to describe the phenomenon of the shift of the main support base of [leftist political parties] to the "[intellectual elite] of the [highly educated]" and their people. It is an analytical term proposed by French economist Thomas Piketty and others, and its counter-concept is "the [Merchant Right] (the right supported by the [business elite] with high incomes). ([Piketty's Institute https://piketty.pse.ens.fr/files/Piketty2018.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Source: 2018 WP "Brahmin Left vs Merchant Right" in Piketty -> 2022 QJE paper (comparing 21 western democracies). It is widely observed that the "[multi-elite system]" where Left = [academic elite] and Right = [income elite]. ([Piketty's Institute https://piketty.pse.ens.fr/files/Piketty2018.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Implication: sensitive to cultural and identity issues, but used to take a critical view of the weakened representation of [lower-educated and lower-income] groups that the traditional left has been responsible for. ([Web Genron https://webgenron.com/articles/bookreview_021?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Counter-concept: Merchant Right. The tendency of the higher-income business class to support the right. The argument is made that the juxtaposition of the two will provide the soil for the old working class to disengage from politics/flow to [right-wing populism]. ([Desai XJP https://desaixjp.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-2450.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Terminological note: Some have pointed out that "Brahmin" refers to the highest caste in India, and therefore should be noted as a metaphor with caste associations (caution against easy stigmatization). ([Web Genron https://webgenron.com/articles/bookreview_021?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Japanese context: the concept itself is based on long-term data from Europe and the U.S. and should be applied with caution to the party and class structure of each country as is. ([OUP Academic https://academic.oup.com/qje/article/137/1/1/6383014?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

For reference: There are many introductions and commentaries (labor policy blogs and book reviews) in Japanese. The following are primary sources for the first published articles and book addenda. ([EU Labor Law Blog https://eulabourlaw.cocolog-nifty.com/blog/2018/04/post-83eb.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
A Cross-Sectional Study (21 Western Democracy, 1948-2020)

Large database (WPID) and summary of QJE paper:** 1960s-80s left = low education and low income support; 2000s-20s "education flipped to the left," while "high income still flows relatively easily to the right "** dual An elite (Brahmin Left vs. Merchant Right) composition is observed.

I guess I should look and experiment myself to tell the story properly, but looking at the results that Claude Code has come up with.

When we imagine clusters, we tend to imagine two-dimensional clusters and assume that most of the points in a cluster are all the points in a cluster, and all of their neighbors are all the points in a cluster.

lines.text: How Cybozu's problem-solving methods were created
[GPT5.icon]
Crisis of 28% turnover (2005): President Aono's book and the publisher's page state that the turnover rate was 28% as of 2005.

Managerial shock (2006): Long interviews with outside media detailed the strays and reflections at the time, including downward revisions to earnings in September and December 2006 (e.g., perception of M&A failure).

[2 billion yen for management study fees | How Cybozu became a company where "100 people, 100 different ways" of working are possible | Diamond Online https://diamond.jp/articles/-/83438?utm_source=chatgpt.com]

Sense of crisis in the background: The turnover rate worsened to about 28% around 2005. While embarking on a review of internal systems and work styles, a "common language for productively discussing and solving problems" became necessary.
[Cybozu's Hybrid Work Media THE HYBRID WORK Cybozu's media dedicated to hybrid work https://hybridwork.cybozu.co.jp/story/cybozu-10years/?utm_source= chatgpt.com]

Manager Training "Flame" (2006) → Declaration of Defeat: In a retrospective of primary internal information, Osamu Yamada clearly states that there was a huge backlash against the training for managers and that "this training was a huge failure" as a summary. The story of how the "type" of discussion = problem-solving method was created is described from this point.
>In the training for managers that we conducted in 2006, we were asked Zen-like questions such as "What kind of company do you want to be? The recipients were like, "I don't know what that means.

> We also had a discussion on the subject of "problems," but I heard that the atmosphere was at its worst, with comments like, "Do you feel the site is a problem?" and "Do you think we are not to be trusted?
> At the end of the training, Mr. Yamada even declared defeat, saying, "This training was a total failure.

[I want to create a team that does not produce "I wish I had done that at that time" - Asami Nakamura, Senior Consultant | Cybozu Teamwork Research Institute https://teamwork.cybozu.co.jp/blog/nakamura-asami.html]
Specifics of the training day (2006/07/01 Sat, President's primary description)

A retrospective by President Yoshihisa Aono (Diamond Online, 12/28/2015). **The "management training" for general managers and PLs was given a preliminary homework assignment, "What kind of company do you want Cybozu to be in the future? However, on the day of the training, the participants exchanged accusations and had a "bitchfest. "** The details of this incident are recorded in the report.
[Management study costs 2 billion yen | How Cybozu became a company where "100 people, 100 different ways" of working are possible | Diamond Online https://diamond.jp/articles/-/83438]

Designer: The development of the in-house method was led by then Vice President Osamu Yamada (stated in the official Teamwork Research Institute article as "Vice President Yamada, who developed the method").
[Cybozu's "Problem Solving Framework" shared in training - Asahi Glass Corporation | Cybozu Teamwork Research Institute https://teamwork.cybozu.co.jp/report/post-1.html]

Operation to gather "facts" from the field: After the crisis phase in 2005, Mr. Yamada conducted **"Zatsudan "** with all employees to uncover facts that were not visible. This became the foundation for the practice of separating "facts/interpretations" in four quadrants.

[Free of charge] "The problem of not knowing what your subordinates are doing when teleworking" can be solved with Zatudan - Chapter 3 of "Management of the Lightest Weight" | Cybozu Style https://cybozushiki.cybozu.co.jp/articles/m005858.html?utm_ source=chatgpt.com]
Initially accepted by development department/penetration took several years: Accepted as "easy to understand" by development department → several years until company-wide penetration
2007-2009: Developed training content (no outside consultants were used, but in-house and self-produced).
2010: A turning point in the "Talk about Teamwork Bar" - a moment when "why teamwork" was verbalized and became clear to me.
Shift from causalism to objectivism: Mr. Aono talks about "what ideal we should strive for rather than the cause of the problem.

[After experiencing a turnover rate of 28%, I realized that "employees leave companies because they want to realize their own ideals" - "The Courage to Be Disliked" by Ichiro Kishimi and Yoshihisa Aono of Cybozu | Cybozu Style https://cybozushiki.cybozu.co.jp/articles/m001277.html?utm _source=chatgpt.com]

Random walk with absorption
[GPT5.icon]

Keywords are [graph-based semi-supervised learning] / [label propagation] / (partially) [absorbing random walks] / [random walk with restart] ([[ Personalized PageRank]). Representative papers are listed by application (1-2 lines each, to the point).

Gaussian Fields & Harmonic Functions (GFHF) - Treats labeled points as boundary conditions (in effect "absorption") and unlabeled values are consistent with the absorption probability of the harmonic function solution = random walk Classical framework where unlabeled values coincide with the absorption probability of the harmonic function solution = random walk. ([mlg.eng.cam.ac.uk https://mlg.eng.cam.ac.uk/zoubin/papers/zgl.pdf])

Learning with Local and Global Consistency (LGC) - Formulation (equivalent to RWR/Individualized PageRank) that spreads and clamps scores with an iterative formula (Y_{t+1}=\alpha S Y_t+(1-\alpha)Y_0). A standard form that is easy to implement. ([proceedings.neurips.cc https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2506-learning-with-local-and-global-consistency.pdf?utm_source= chatgpt.com])

Label Propagation (Zhu & Ghahramani, 2002) - Basic algorithm for iteratively spreading labels on similarity graphs (with and without clamp variants). ([mlg.eng.cam.ac.uk https://mlg.eng.cam.ac.uk/zoubin/papers/CMU-CALD-02-107.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Rendezvous algorithm (Azran, 2007) - an explicit "absorbing RW" model that puts labeled nodes into an absorbing state and gives a multi-class distribution with probabilities of absorption from each unlabeled node. ([mlg.eng.cam.ac.uk https://mlg.eng.cam.ac.uk/pub/pdf/Azr07.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Partially Absorbing Random Walks (PARW, NIPS 2012) - A generalization that allows continuous adjustment of absorption rates; integrates GFHF/LGC/PageRank systems in the same framework. ([ee.columbia.edu https://www.ee.columbia.edu/~zgli/papers/NIPS2012_PARW.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Random Walk with Restart / Personalized PageRank - Fast computation and application of RW with Restart (((I-\alpha S)^{-1}) form). Frequently used as a foundation for semi-supervised classification and as a proximate theory. ([ucilnica.fri.uni-lj.si https://ucilnica.fri.uni-lj.si/pluginfile.php/1212/course/section/1199/Tong%20et%20al%20-%20Fast%20random% 20walk%20with%20restart%20and%20its%20applications%2C%202006.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Adsorption / Modified Adsorption (Baluja et al.; Talukdar & Crammer) - A diffusion/absorption type derivation method that has been put to practical use in industrial scale graphs and its optimized version MAD.([archives.iw3c2.org https://archives.iw3c2.org/www2008/papers/pdf/p895-svakumarA.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

In summary, the update formula you are using is of the LGC/RWR family, and the interpretation of the label as a "stop" is a direct reference to GFHF/Azran/PARW. If necessary, I can write down exactly which formula corresponds to which.

I looked at what ChatGPT had written and said a lot of things like, "That's not what I was trying to make," and I got something that wasn't what I was trying to make.
→[Subjective Interest Estimation System].
I'll fatten this one up, too.
[https://gyazo.com/a25fd0e5c7088e42f7a19f7cf42e09ec]
1: A Chat log consists of multiple chunks
The elementary form of that chunk is "pairs of human reactions to AI statements."
If you are using RAG chunking for simple text, you can cut by length without assuming structure, but if the target data is chat, it is better to maintain that structure.
In truth, it might be better to have the "context of the story to that point" before the pair, but once you do it naively
2: 0~N information is extracted from this pair
What information we want to extract here needs to be verbalized.
If you want to extract useful information, you need to verbalize what you find useful.
End-users, of course, cannot verbalize it.
So I let GPT5, who read my external brain, think about it, and then I actually used the prompts to see what was extracted and give feedback back and update it.
code:prompt
You are an interview analyst. Read the following Q (AI question) and A (human answer),
Output 0 or more "UsefulInfo" in JSON.
If the probability of being useful is low, then 0 cases can be extracted (hallucination prohibited, reduce noise).
Axis of usefulness rating (100 points each):

- One-Step-Forward (0-100 points): It should be a specific insight that corresponds to "one step beyond the knowledge we have now" rather than a general idea that is likely to be known to the respondent or reader. Stale layman's ideas receive a score of 0.
- Bridge (0-100 points): New connections (contrast, causality, inclusion, association, etc. "non-similarity") between different themes/concepts are included.

- Actionability (0-100 points): The degree to which specific actions and conditions/constraints that can be tried are clearly stated. Abstract criticisms (e.g., "lack of specificity") receive low scores.
- Falsifiable (0-100 points): To the extent that it is possible to mention counter-example verification and measurement methods.

- Experienced (0-100 points): To the extent that it is based on the speaker's own specific experience. References to actual social issues" is not enough. Emphasis should be placed on the speaker's actual experiences and observations.
Notes:
- Simple position statements ("I agree" or "I think it's a good idea") are not useful information.
- Personal attitude statements only ("I don't care") are not useful information.

Subjective Interest Estimation System
For situations like [public information AI], where a large number of objects are embedded in a vector space
I want to extract from [the extracted findings]([a large number of objects]) what the analyst finds interesting
However, this "interestingness" is subjective and what one finds interesting is not known
[subjective interest].
Analysts have not been able to verbalize it.
So AI has to find out "what the analyst finds interesting" through dialogue with the analyst.
Perhaps "one step outside what we already know."
Related: [I can only accept knowledge that is one step ahead of what I have now].

Random presentation -> Rate the "interestingness" on 5 levels from -2 to +2, use the data to estimate the "interestingness" of the unknowns in the space of embedding opinions [Gaussian regression], +1SD, and present it in a UCB-1 style [Trade-offs between use and exploration]. exploration] and present the results.
[** ver.2][GPT5.icon]
Objective.
From the extracted findings, the analyst himself/herself automatically selects the ones he/she finds "interesting. However, "[Interestingness]" is not known in advance, but is indicated by [subject].
method
First, the findings are presented at random and rated on a scale of -2 to +2 on a 5-point scale of "interestingness.

Each finding is represented by an embedded vector. Based on the evaluated points, estimate the **expected score (μ) and uncertainty (σ) ** for the unrated findings by [Gaussian regression] (or its approximation).
For the next candidates to be presented, priority is given to those with high UCB = μ + 1σ (= good & unknown), and points are deducted for those too similar to ensure diversity.
By repeating this process, the accuracy of presenting "interesting findings" tailored to the person's subjective viewpoint is automatically improved.
PS[nishio.icon]
It is interesting when used by one person, but when used by multiple people, it can be like "Mr. A thinks it's funny, but Mr. B doesn't think it's funny, explain what's funny.
[Cartographer]-like mechanism

[GPT5.icon]
To put it plainly, this is how it works.
word summary
The criteria for what people find "interesting" are unknown at first, so they learn little by little.

We randomly show the candidates and ask the participants to rate them on a 5-point scale, and then predict the "interestingness" of the candidates in the embedded space based on the assumption that similar opinions will receive similar scores.
From that forecast, present the next one that looks good & still uncertain in a balanced way.
Why do this?
Interestingness" is subjective and varies from person to person. We can't set the rules ahead of time.
So we need to learn interactively (small amount of evaluation -> next presentation will be smarter).
Core of the mechanism
1. embedding
Vectorize each opinion and create a "the closer the content, the closer the vector" map.
2. evaluation data (-2 to +2)
We will show you a few random cases and record your "interestingness" as a score.
3. forecasting (e.g., Gaussian process regression)
Using the points you have evaluated as clues, you can find the points on the map that you have not yet seen.
Forecast Interest (average) μ
Uncertainty (width) σ
Estimate the
4. strategy of presentation (UCB)
The next candidate to show is the one with high μ + 1σ (= UCB):
High μ → Probably interesting (utilization)
σ is large → still uncertain (search)
If you choose one with a large sum of these two, you can achieve a balance between utilization and exploration.
Actual flow (steps)
1. first present 20 to 30 cases at random and ask them to rate them from -2 to +2.
2. use that evaluation to predict the interestingness in the embedding space (compute μ, σ).
3. produce the next 5 cases in order of increasing UCB = μ + 1σ (also add [diversity penalty] to prevent too much similarity).
Not in the original memo.[nishio.icon]

4. update the forecast each time the number of evaluations increases → the presentation becomes smarter and smarter.
Intuitive metaphor
It's like looking for a good restaurant on an unexplored map.
**Mix in a few hole-in-the-wall places that seem to have a high **reputation (μ)** as well as a few that have little **information (big sigma).
This way, you can get to the good stores faster while reducing oversight.
term mini-dictionary
Embedded: a numerical vector of the meaning of a sentence. The closer the topic, the closer the point.
Gaussian Process Regression (GP): a method to estimate **mean (μ) and uncertainty (σ)** under the smoothness assumption that close points tend to have similar scores.
UCB (Upper Confidence Bound, [Upper Confidence Bound]): UCB = µ + coefficient x σ. An index to choose with emphasis on both good & unknown. Here the coefficient = 1 (= +1SD).
Evaluation rules for immediate use (field notes)
Scale: -2 (not interesting at all) to +2 (very interesting)
If in doubt, 0 is OK (does not interfere with learning).
The same item is sometimes redisplayed for subjective blur estimation (quality improvement).
Frequently Asked Questions
Q: Why "+1σ"?

A: The larger the coefficient, the more "search-oriented" and the smaller the coefficient, the more "utilization-oriented". 1 is easy to handle for MVP. The coefficient can be adjusted later in the range of 1.0 to 2.0.
Q: Does it have to be GP?
A: Approximation (random features x linear regression) is sufficient. A lightweight version is OK to start with.
